candidates.title: Mapping machine learning applications across the food value chain through a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
candidates.abstract: Abstract Food industry plays major role in public health, economic and environmental sustainability. Integration of machine learning (ML) is increasingly reshaping elements like safety protocols, quality management and supply chain optimization, though outcomes vary substantially by context and scale. This paper comprehensively synthesizes the ML applications by employing a systematic literature review (SLR) and a bibliometric analysis of 234 peer-reviewed articles published since 2014 and identifies prominent ML techniques like neural networks, support vector machines, and ensemble techniques. Various applications of these methods are food processing, fraud detection, personalized nutrition, and predictive maintenance. Collaborative pattern along with possible research directions are predicted using keywords co-occurrence and co-authorship network. Explainable AI (XAI), federated learning (FL) along with ethical rules are essential to ensure implementation and navigate AI driven revolution in food sector. Deep learning models have achieved very high classification accuracy in controlled food-quality trials, while early ML-driven dynamic-pricing pilots in SME grocery settings have reported substantial reductions in food waste and modest revenue gains; however, these results are context-specific and remain unconfirmed across broader, resource-constrained SME contexts.

candidates.title: LangBiTe: model-driven bias testing of text-to-text large language models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have rapidly gained popularity across a wide range of applications, from customer support to content generation and decision support systems. However, LLMs have also been found to exhibit social biases, reflecting and amplifying stereotypes and prejudices present in their training data. Such biases can lead to harmful outcomes, particularly in sensitive domains. Addressing these risks is essential to ensure that the adoption of LLMs contributes positively to society without reinforcing existing inequalities. To facilitate a continuous, robust ethical assessment of text-to-text LLMs, we propose LangBiTe, a model-driven solution to configure and automate the testing of ethical biases. LangBiTe may uncover biases embedded within the LLM-based components of a software system and thus motivate adjustments, or the selection of a different LLM in line with the ethical requirements. The model-driven approach makes both the requirements specification and the test generation platform-independent and provides end-to-end traceability between the requirements and their assessment. Moreover, LangBiTe includes capabilities for an LLM-assisted generation of bias-testing datasets. We have implemented an open-source tool set, available on GitHub, to support the application of our approach. Finally, we present a series of case studies where LangBiTe was applied to unveil biases in several, popular online text-to-text LLMs, thus demonstrating the effectiveness of its diverse functionalities.

candidates.title: Emergence of Goal‐Directed Behaviors via Active Inference With Self‐Prior
candidates.abstract: Infants often exhibit goal-directed behaviors, such as reaching for a sensory stimulus, even when no external reward criterion is provided. These intrinsically motivated behaviors facilitate spontaneous exploration and learning of the body and environment during early developmental stages. Although computational modeling can offer insight into the mechanisms underlying such behaviors, many existing studies on intrinsic motivation focus primarily on how exploration contributes to acquiring external rewards. In this paper, we propose a novel density model for an agent's own multimodal sensory experiences, called the "self-prior," and investigate whether it can autonomously induce goal-directed behavior. Integrated within an active inference framework based on the free energy principle, the self-prior generates behavioral references purely from an intrinsic process that minimizes mismatches between average past sensory experiences and current observations. This mechanism is also analogous to the acquisition and utilization of a body schema through continuous interaction with the environment. We examine this approach in a simulated environment and confirm that the agent spontaneously reaches toward a tactile stimulus. Our study implements intrinsically motivated behavior shaped by the agent's own sensory experiences, demonstrating the spontaneous emergence of intentional behavior during early development. SUMMARY: Suggests a computational model for early intentional behavior, integrating body-schema formation and goal-directed actions under the free energy principle. Introduces a self-prior as an internal density model that drives the emergence of goal-directed behaviors without external rewards. Demonstrates spontaneous reaching for a sticker by minimizing mismatches between observed multimodal sensory inputs and the empirically acquired self-prior.

candidates.title: Record stack durability in industrial solid oxide steam electrolysis through operational control
candidates.abstract: Solid oxide steam electrolysis offers the highest electrical efficiency for hydrogen production, yet wide-scale deployment remains constrained by durability. Here, we show that long-term stack durability can be strongly influenced by operating strategy, achieving 25,000 h of steam electrolysis operation in a full 70-cell solid oxide electrolysis cell stack under frequency-dependent electrochemical operation (AC:DC). This experiment represents, to our knowledge, the longest and lowest degradation operation reported for a full stack. The stack enters a stabilized regime with an average voltage degradation rate of 0.05 % kh⁻¹ (0.65 mV kh⁻¹ per cell) sustained for 22,000 h after initial conditioning. The behavior is evaluated against initial DC operation, prior full-stack benchmarks, impedance evolution, and post-test microstructural signatures. Periodic polarity inversion between electrolysis and fuel-cell modes modulates electrochemical polarization and heat generation, consistent with mitigating thermal and electrochemical gradients that develop during sustained DC electrolysis. Stack-level impedance evolution and post-mortem microstructural analysis demonstrate stabilization of electrochemical performance and suppression of degradation signatures commonly observed under DC operation, indicating that key degradation pathways are not activated under AC:DC operation. By shifting durability control from materials to operational strategy, AC:DC operation offers a scalable pathway toward long-lived solid oxide electrolysis for economically competitive green hydrogen production. Demonstration of a long and low degradation solid oxide steam electrolysis experiment for a full SOEC stack, achieving 25,000 hours of operation through AC:DC operation showing potential for low-cost green hydrogen production.

candidates.title: Large language models as travel co-planners: the GIFT model of youth–AI interaction
candidates.abstract: This study examines how members of Generation Z and Generation Alpha perceive and use LLMs in tourism planning. Drawing on six age-specific focus groups with 57 participants (26 Generation Alpha pupils aged 11–14 and 31 Generation Z BSc students aged 20–24) conducted in Budapest, Hungary, the study uses a qualitative, Grounded Theory–informed approach to explore prior use, anticipated practices, credibility assessments, and the meanings attached to LLMs. Participants in both cohorts were familiar with digital technologies and valued fast, personalized services, but their accounts differed in decision-making autonomy, social embeddedness, and evaluative practices. Generation Alpha participants more often positioned LLMs as an exploratory assistant within family-based decision structures, whereas Generation Z participants more frequently described comparing or verifying AI-generated outputs through other sources and social input. These patterns are better understood as different modes of credibility assessment and reliance than as simple differences in trust. The resulting GIFT ( Generational Interpretations of Future-oriented Technologies ) framework conceptualizes youth–AI interaction in tourism planning as context-dependent, with LLMs serving as cognitive support tools and potential co-creators. GIFT is presented as an exploratory framework grounded in this sample rather than as a universal theory. The study links human–AI interaction to the social contexts in which young people make travel decisions and offers implications for tourism professionals, educators, and AI developers.

candidates.title: What If We Work Together? Fostering Reflections on Designer Inclusion in Open Source Software Through Speculative Design
candidates.abstract: Open source software (OSS) often prioritizes technical functionality over usability and UX design. This imbalance limits OSS adoption among broader, non-technical users. Key underlying factors contributing to this issue are the shortage of design expertise in OSS and a dominant developer-centric mindset. To address these persistent issues, we explore the potential of speculative design as a catalyst for transforming the OSS community’s mindset towards a more designer-inclusive environment. Our design was informed by an analysis of online forums, which revealed designers’ motivations and challenges when contributing to OSS. Guided by these insights, we created two speculative societies, Husia (collectivist) and Reetar (individualist), in which designers are valued for different reasons and their work incorporated in different ways. Through a user study with 12 OSS practitioners (seven designers and five developers), we found that our speculative societies provoked participants’ rich and critical reflections on OSS values, the root causes of challenges, and proposed actions. Our work provides insights into how speculative design can be used in the practical, sociotechnical context of OSS to stimulate critical reflection, improve awareness, and yield recommendations for fostering an equitable, sustainable, and inclusive OSS environment.

candidates.title: Generating Project-Specific Test Cases with Requirement Validation Intention
candidates.abstract: Test cases are valuable assets for maintaining software quality. State-of-the-art automated test generation techniques typically focus on maximizing program branch coverage or translating focal methods into test code. However, in contrast to branch coverage or code-to-test translation, practical tests are written out of the need to validate whether a requirement has been fulfilled. Specifically, a test usually reflects a developer’s validation intention for a particular scenario of a program function, regarding (1) what is the test scenario of a program function? and (2) what is the expected behavior under such a scenario? Without taking such intention into account, generated tests are less likely to be adopted in practice. In this work, we propose IntentionTest, which generates project-specific tests given the description of validation intention. The design is motivated by two insights: (1) rationale insight : the description of validation intention regarding scenario description and behavioral expectation, compared to coverage and focal code, carries more crucial information about what to test ; and (2) technical insight : practical test code exhibits high duplication, indicating that existing tests are highly reusable for how to test . Therefore, IntentionTest adopts a retrieval-and-edit manner. First, given a focal code and a description of validation intention consisting of a test objective with test precondition and expected results, IntentionTest retrieves a reusable test in the project as the test reference. Then, IntentionTest edits the test reference with an LLM regarding the validation intention toward the target test. To help the target test include a project-specific test prefix and a relevant assertion, IntentionTest further explores the software project to identify crucial code facts (i.e., relevant API/code to call and global variables to refer to in the test) as important context for the test generation. We extensively evaluate IntentionTest against four baselines (TELPA, DA, ChatTester, and EvoSuite) on 3,680 test cases from 12 open-source projects. Compared to state-of-the-art baselines, with a given validation intention, IntentionTest can (1) generate tests far more semantically relevant to ground-truth tests by (i) achieving common mutation scores 28.1% to 37.6% higher and (ii) achieving common coverage ratios 16.9% to 23.9% higher; and (2) achieve successful-pass rates 23.7% to 49.0% higher.

candidates.title: Large testing of AI-based camera traps on a forest defoliating pest in Europe
candidates.abstract: Background Recent advances in AI-based surveillance technologies have shifted agricultural pest monitoring from reactive to proactive, yet their application to forest pests remains limited despite the need for efficient monitoring across large, remote and difficult-to-access forest landscapes. The pine processionary moth, Thaumetopoea pityocampa , is one of the most damaging forest pests in the Mediterranean region and a species undergoing climate-driven distributional and phenological shifts. Methods We evaluated the performance of the AI-based camera system for monitoring the insect under field conditions. Automated traps were compared with conventional traps across four European countries (France, Italy, Portugal, and Slovenia), encompassing contrasting habitats and population densities. We assessed trapping efficiency, automated image recognition accuracy, probability of early detection, relationships between adult trap catch and local nest density, environmental drivers of flight activity, and non-target captures. Results Automated traps consistently outperformed conventional traps by catching significantly more moths in France, Italy and Portugal, while demonstrating the same positive trend under the low-density conditions found in Slovenia. The smart trap also detected adult activity earlier and significantly increased the probability of detection during the first weeks of the flight season. Manual validation confirmed excellent performance of the AI recognition algorithm, with near-perfect precision, recall, F1-score, and overall accuracy throughout the flight season. For both trap types, adult trap catches showed positive and statistically significant relationships with subsequent nest density, indicating that higher catches were associated with greater larval infestation. The meteorological data provided synchronously by automated traps showed that temperature generally promoted moth flight activity, whereas high relative humidity hindered it. In addition, automated traps significantly reduced non-target catch compared to conventional traps. Conclusions Overall, this study provides the first large-scale evaluation of an AI-based camera trap for monitoring the pine processionary moth and demonstrates its considerable potential to improve forest pest surveillance.

candidates.title: DexWrist: A Robotic Wrist for Constrained and Dynamic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Development of dexterous manipulation hardware has primarily focused on hands and grippers. However, these end-effectors are often paired with bulky and highly stiff wrists that limit performance in human environments. More recent designs have adopted backdrivable actuation, but are still difficult to model and control due to coupled kinematics or high mechanical inertia from heavy links. We present DexWrist, a compact robotic wrist combining quasi-direct-drive actuation with a decoupled parallel kinematic mechanism to advance manipulation in highly constrained environments and enable dynamic, contact-rich tasks. It delivers 3.75$\pm$0.05 Nm rated torque, 0.33$\pm$0.06 Nm backdrive torque, 10.15$\pm$1.34 Hz torque bandwidth, $\pm 40^\circ$ ROM in both DOFs, and a diagonal velocity-constraint Jacobian (one-to-one motor-to-DOF mapping) in a 0.97 kg package. In practice, these properties increase workspace in clutter and stabilize contact without finely tuned admittance control. We evaluate DexWrist as a drop-in upgrade in simulation and on three robot arms across constrained and contact-rich tasks. In learned policy evaluations on the AgileX PiPER and UR3e, DexWrist achieved 50-76% relative improvements in success rate and reduced autonomous task completion times by 3-5x; on a torque-controlled Franka FR3, where a strong joint-impedance baseline already succeeds, it still completed the task 1.4x faster. Project page and videos: https://martinpeticco.com/dexwrist

candidates.title: The WoKaS-Iso database: workflow for a global compilation of oxygen-18 and deuterium records in karst springs and cave drip water for enhanced understanding of karst systems
candidates.abstract: Abstract. For analysing karst hydrogeological systems, observations of karst springs and cave drips are considered indispensable. In addition to hydrometric observations, knowing the oxygen and hydrogen stable isotope ratios has improved the understanding of vadose zone and aquifer dynamics, likewise supporting system characterisation and modelling. However, limited accessibility and high costs of the analysis of stable isotopes in karst aquifers have hindered progress in karst research and impeded the accurate understanding of karst processes especially when it comes to comparative or large-scale studies. In this study, we present our workflow to compile the WoKaS-Iso database, the first extensive collection of time series data for Oxygen-18 and Deuterium isotopes in karst springs and cave drip water from diverse sources, encompassing publications, theses, reports, online archives, and collaborative initiatives worldwide. The database incorporates data sourced from 236 springs and 74 caves, comprising in total 997 time series (379 time series for the springs and 618 time series for the cave drip water). These datasets provide coverage across significant karst regions globally, spanning China, the USA, Europe, the Middle East, and Australia. Within datasets, 79% for springs and 68% for cave drip water exhibit resolutions finer than monthly intervals. In addition, by integrating isotopic records with ancillary environmental variables including spring discharge, cave drip rate, precipitation, and rainwater isotopes, the database offers a more comprehensive perspective on hydrological behaviours in karst aquifers, hence advancing hydrogeological characterisation and modelling. The WoKaS-Iso database not only deepens the understanding of the complex systems but also promotes sustainable water resource management as well as the potential to foster collaborative research. The database can be accessed at: https://doi.org/10.25532/OPARA-909.

candidates.title: From OSS to Open Source AI: an Exploratory Study of Collaborative Development Paradigm Divergence
candidates.abstract: AI development is embracing open-source paradigm, but the fundamental distinction between AI models and traditional software artifacts may lead to a divergent open-source development paradigm with different collaborative practices, which remains unexplored. We therefore bridge the knowledge gap by quantifying and characterizing the differences in the collaborative development paradigms of traditional open source software (OSS) and open source AI models (OSM), and investigating the underlying factors that may drive these distinctions. We collect 1,428,792 OSS repositories from GitHub and 1,440,527 OSM repositories from HF Hub, and conduct comprehensive statistical, social network and content analyses to measure and understand the differences in collaboration intensity, collaboration openness, and user innovation across the two development paradigms, complementing these quantitative results with semi-structured interviews. In consequence, we find that compared to OSS development paradigm, the OSM development paradigm exhibits significantly lower collaboration intensity; lower collaboration openness regarding direct contribution while persisting relatively open knowledge exchange; and a divergence toward adaptive utilization user-innovation rather than collaborative improvement. Through semi-structured interviews, we further elucidate the socio-technical factors underlying these differences. These findings reveal the paradigmatic divergence in open source development between traditional OSS and OSM across three critical dimensions of open source collaboration and potential underlying factors, shedding light on how to improve collaborative work techniques and practices within the context of AI development.

candidates.title: Social chatbots and character: Mind-modelling, mimetics, and postdigital misperception
candidates.abstract: This article examines how users cognitively process social chatbot output as a novel form of participatory, generative “character,” co-produced through human–AI interaction. Reporting on the results of empirical research on user responses to the social chatbot platform character.ai, it shows how cognitive stylistic and narratological approaches to character can be utilised but also must be developed to analyse and theorise users’ experience of and interaction with generative AI agents. It makes specific contributions to cognitive stylistics, rhetorical narratology, character studies, and research on gen AI chatbots by: (1) illustrating how the concept of mind-modelling can used to analyse the ways in which users linguistically anthropomorphise social chatbots; (2) developing two new audience response types – transmimetic and hypermimetic – to respectively capture ways in which users assess chatbots against prior knowledge of characters across media and cases where chatbots appear so convincingly human that users question their ontological status; (3) proposing the concept of ‘postdigital misperception’ to reflect the way that users of AI can misattribute the ontological origin of an LLM’s output. The article demonstrates how social chatbots are reshaping how users understand character, agency, and reality in interactive, participatory and generative digital contexts and argues that social chatbots epitomise postdigital experience in blurring the distinction between the digital and non-digital as well as fictional and real.

candidates.title: Edge AI and IoT-enabled livestock intrusion detection and automated farm protection using YOLOv8s and MQTT-enabled event notification
candidates.abstract: Precision livestock farming relies on intelligent sensing and automated decision-making to reduce economic losses from livestock intrusion. Existing systems typically handle visual detection or IoT notification separately, limiting real-time autonomous response. This paper presents an Edge AI and IoT framework that integrates YOLOv8s-based cattle detection with MQTT-driven event communication and automated physical actuation. The system combines a real-time object detection engine, Python-based orchestration, MQTT communication, an ESP32 controller, cloud notification services, and acoustic deterrence into a unified cyber-physical architecture. The model was trained on a Roboflow cattle dataset using transfer learning under Ultralytics YOLOv8. Experimental results show a Precision of 0.8039, Recall of 0.6846, F1-score of 0.7394, mAP@50 of 0.8094, and mAP@50:95 of 0.5347. Average inference latency was 132.16 ms, while MQTT transmission required only 0.21 ms. This study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating visual perception, IoT communication, automated notification, and real-time physical intervention for autonomous livestock intrusion monitoring.

candidates.title: Vision-language model guided three-dimensional segmentation for automated and high-fidelity strawberry point cloud reconstruction
candidates.abstract: For strawberry picking or inspection robots, acquiring three-dimensional (3D) point clouds of strawberries from single-view red, green, and blue (RGB) images or point cloud data is crucial. Current methods rely on a large-scale three-dimensional point cloud library of strawberries. To obtain this library, existing methods mainly rely on Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), point cloud registration, and segmentation, which are costly and time-consuming. This research proposes a multi-view driven 3D segmentation framework based on three-dimensional Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and a vision-language model (VLM) to enable efficient and accurate reconstruction of complete strawberry point clouds. Firstly, an image acquisition device and software are developed, enabling rapid capture of images from multiple viewpoints. Secondly, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) is fine-tuned using Low-Rank Adaptation and its bounding-box prompts are provided by the Vision Transformer for Open-World Localization (OWL-ViT) with “strawberry” concept as the prompt for OWL-ViT; thus, accurate strawberry segmentation masks on raw images are obtained as supervision masks. Finally, a joint loss function is proposed that integrates RGB color consistency loss and edge-aware loss to optimize the 3D segmentation weight vector iteratively. On a self-constructed dataset containing 400 strawberries, each captured from 144 RGB viewpoints, experiments show that the proposed method achieves a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 89.44% and a mean Accuracy (mAcc) of 99.40% in the 3D segmentation task, while maintaining high computational efficiency. Additionally, the superiority of the proposed method is further validated through generalization experiments on several complex scenes (e.g., bonsai, kitchen, garden) from a publicly available dataset.

candidates.title: From Individual to Lineage Identity: Huizhou Merchants and the Rise of Genealogies in Ming China
candidates.abstract: Abstract This article examines how Huizhou merchants shaped their identities during their economic ascent from the fifteenth century onward. Because commerce carried a stigma in Confucian ideology, they shifted the basis of self-presentation from mercantile success to moral excellence. This produced a competition in virtue, where the moral capital accumulated in a single lifetime could not rival that amassed across generations. Merchants therefore redirected identity claims from personal virtue to membership in lineages where virtue had been cultivated over generations. In doing so, they moved the foundation of identity from individual achievement to collective lineage affiliation. This shift provides a new explanation for the rise of lineages and genealogies from the perspective of identity formation. By underscoring the initiative, creativity, and adaptability of merchants in driving these changes, the article also repositions them from the cultural margins to the center of identity-making in late imperial China.

candidates.title: When the Mas’ Done: The Limits of Carnival in The Dragon Can’t Dance
candidates.abstract: In Earl Lovelace's The Dragon Can't Dance, Carnival is at once both a resistant cultural inheritance and a politically unstable form of rebellion. This essay argues that while Carnival gives the dispossessed people of Calvary Hill a language through which to assert their personhood, it ultimately misdirects revolutionary potential to temporary, ephemeral forms. Through Aldrick's dragon, Fisheye's steelband, and the failed revolt of the People's Liberation Army, Lovelace exposes the limits of resistance when it remains contained within a spectacle. Through Philo, Sylvia, and the changing people of the Corner, Lovelace further shows that symbolic rebellion is incompatible with the material demands of hunger, work, and survival. Drawing on the research of Frantz Fanon, James C. Scott, Garth L. Green, Emily Zobel Marshall, Max Farrar, Guy Farrar, and Richard McGuire, this essay explores the phenomena of Carnival through equal parts sociology and post-colonial study. Further, it examines the position of Carnival in Caribbean literature and history.

candidates.title: Enhancing synchronous patterned motion tracking and latency reduction through avatar prediction and visualization
candidates.abstract: Enabling online virtual reality (VR) users to move naturally and contextually within their environment presents transformative possibilities for enhancing human motion prediction accuracy and fostering a deeper sense of connection in shared remote settings. Latency in motion tracking remains a significant challenge, as it directly impacts the user’s sense of presence and engagement in VR environments. This study investigates the integration of real-time human pose tracking and motion prediction techniques to reconstruct context-aware, skeleton-based motion sequences from historical data.The findings highlight that improved motion tracking and prediction significantly enhance immersion and social connectivity in VR, particularly in interactive scenarios such as online dancing. By leveraging historical motion sequences and machine learning models, this research develops methods to accurately render human motion in avatar or mesh formats, enabling seamless synchronization of movements with dynamic contexts, including music beats in paired dance scenarios. The integration of predictive modelling and advanced learning techniques offers a robust framework for creating realistic and engaging virtual interactions. This research contributes to advancing immersive user experiences in networked VR applications by providing a novel approach to tracking, reconstructing, and predicting human motions. The outcomes emphasize the potential of enhancing user connection, enjoyment, and realism in virtual environments, paving the way for enriched interactive applications in areas such as virtual performances, remote collaboration, and social VR experiences.

candidates.title: Autonomous Industrial Inspection with Quadruped Robots: A Systematic Literature Review
candidates.abstract: Quadruped robots are increasingly used for industrial inspection because they can traverse stairs, clutter, and uneven terrain built for people. This paper presents a Systematic Literature Review (SLR), following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, of autonomous inspection with quadruped robots validated on physical hardware. Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library were searched between 13 and 16 August 2026 for studies published from 2018 to 2026. Of 745 unique records and 1 study found through citation searching, 88 full-text reports were assessed against explicit eligibility criteria and an eight-criterion quality rubric, three criteria of which (mission focus, autonomy integration, and environmental fidelity) acted as eligibility gates; 32 studies were included. They were synthesized narratively by mission control, localization and mapping, navigation, active inspection, and validation approach. Robots reach inspection targets in real facilities, mostly on commercial platforms with vendor or open-source LiDAR localization, but only 4 of the 32 studies let inspection results change the mission, only 3 quantify localization accuracy on hardware, 14 report no statistics over repeated runs, and 27 provide no public code or data. The evidence is limited by single-reviewer selection, short deployments, heterogeneous metrics, and a likely bias toward successful demonstrations.

candidates.title: Design and Evaluation of a Cost-Effective Autonomous Outdoor Cleaning Robot for Public Park Environments
candidates.abstract: This study presents a practical approach to developing a prototype outdoor cleaning robot with reduced hardware and software complexity. While indoor cleaning robots are widely adopted, their outdoor counterparts remain costly and less accessible due to unstructured environments and increased system complexity. To address this, we retrofitted an off-the-shelf manual sweeper with minimal hardware: a single 3D LiDAR and a compact onboard computer running an open-source autonomy software stack. This LiDAR-centric design reduces hardware and software integration complexity while using the integrated IMU of the LiDAR for motion compensation. We focus on adapting three key autonomy modules, mapping, localization, and planning, for semi-structured park environments characterized by dense vegetation and GNSS-denied conditions. A consistent and loop-closed pointcloud map was generated using a LiDAR SLAM framework. Map-based pose initialization and LiDAR scan matching were evaluated under the tested conditions. Bidirectional path-following behavior was demonstrated through lanelet-based planning adapted for shared narrow paths. A field trial demonstrated autonomous execution of the predefined cleaning route, with a loop-closure residual of 0.072 m, low covariance-derived lateral uncertainty, and a mean deviation from the lanelet-centerline reference trajectory of approximately 0.14 m. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a low-complexity LiDAR-centric autonomy architecture for the tested outdoor cleaning scenario.

candidates.title: Unlocking electric vehicle flexibility in microgrids via lightweight on-charger coordination
candidates.abstract: The large-scale integration of electric vehicles could provide substantial flexibility for balancing renewable energy in microgrids, yet this potential remains largely constrained by uncoordinated charging. Here, we show that on-board chargers can be transformed into intelligent agents to unlock this flexibility through distributed vehicle-grid coordination. To enable such coordination under practical hardware constraints, we develop a distributed framework that embeds edge intelligence into resource-constrained chargers for autonomous charging optimization. Validated on a high-fidelity hardware-in-the-loop platform capturing microgrid cyber-physical dynamics, experimental results demonstrate that our framework reduces memory consumption by 96.1% and communication overhead by 74.3% compared to the traditional distributed coordination scheme. Moreover, unlocking this hardware-level flexibility achieves a 10.8% profit increase over the current uncoordinated situation. Importantly, the proposed framework promises profound economic, environmental, and social benefits for the future energy landscape from 2025 to 2040. Uncoordinated electric vehicle charging strains microgrids, yet advanced control exceeds charger hardware limits. Here, the authors develop a lightweight on-charger coordination framework that unlocks vehicle flexibility with low memory and communication needs.

candidates.title: ROS2 Coordination Middleware for Multi-robot Systems
candidates.abstract: Abstract ROS2 provides robust communication primitives for robotic systems but lacks standardized support for multi-robot coordination. Consequently, coordination logic must be implemented manually, often relying on centralized control, global knowledge of agents, or synchronized execution—assumptions that do not hold in open and dynamic environments. We present a lightweight ROS2 coordination middleware that enables fully decentralized, anonymous, and asynchronous multi-robot coordination. The middleware is organized as a logical tree of ROS2 nodes, eliminating single points of failure and supporting dynamic membership. Rather than relying on a global clock, coordination is expressed through a total order over exchanged messages, ensuring deterministic behavior with respect to the established order despite delays and different execution times. We provide an open-source high-level API that abstracts coordination from ROS2 communication details. Two classical coordination scenarios are implemented to establish consensus in a fully asynchronous and anonymous setting, demonstrating the applicability of the proposed approach.

candidates.title: A Generalized Architecture for Orchestrating Assembly in a Self-organizing Production Cell
candidates.abstract: Abstract Smart manufacturing is becoming an increasingly important topic in both current research and industry. In the production of customized products, assembly steps are not identical across products but must instead be dynamically orchestrated for suitable robot teams at runtime. In this paper, we present a general architecture for the automated planning and the coordinated, autonomous execution of such multi-robot orchestrations in a self-organizing production cell where robots can autonomously team up at flexible positions by adjusting their positions up to a certain degree. Our architecture enables conflict-free orchestration across multiple problem contexts using shared resources (i.e., robots, carts, tools, products, parts in the cell) in a real-world production cell. We validate our architecture in three of many distinct problem contexts: (1) the provisioning of necessary bulk materials for the production robots, (2) the provisioning of intermediate products and their assembly into target products by the robot team, and (3) the structured release of production resources for subsequent production steps. We evaluated these three contexts both in a virtual representation of the production cell and on the real system. Our investigations include validation of our concepts in the three problem contexts including proof-of-concept scenarios that can occur during production, dealing with isolated and interwoven problems, supported with comprehensive video documentation. Finally, we discuss further research directions.

candidates.title: Foundation Models for Autonomous Space Robotics: Architectures, Physical Adaptation, and Validation
candidates.abstract: Space robots must interpret tasks and act despite unfamiliar dynamics, difficult sensing conditions, and limited opportunities for human intervention. Foundation models offer reusable perceptual and behavioral knowledge, but their value depends on how that knowledge reaches physical execution. This critical review follows space-specific requirements through perception, prediction, planning, and action to deployment and validation, emphasizing orbital manipulation and proximity operations. Terrestrial comparisons establish benefits of particular pretraining stages and model interfaces; their transfer to space dynamics and constrained onboard operation remains insufficiently tested. Event cameras offer timely motion observations across strong illumination contrasts, while spiking neural networks provide possible routes to sparse local computation. We examine how sensor degradation, state estimation and computing choices affect feedback and recovery. Higher action throughput need not yield fresher feedback; lower processor power can also coexist with higher energy per inference. We organize validation as an iterative sim-to-ground-to-space pathway, connecting physical tests with telemetry-based diagnosis and closed-loop revalidation. A satellite-capture example links observations to approach, contact and recovery, while a corresponding protocol separates generalization from adaptation with limited target-domain interaction. These comparisons identify what models already contribute and the physical evidence needed to support autonomous space operation.

candidates.title: Coordinating a Robot Swarm in a Warehouse by Aggregate Programming: A Case Study
candidates.abstract: Abstract Multi-robot systems (MRS) are becoming increasingly relevant within diverse application domains, including warehouse logistics, where robots are in charge of moving and storing crates, by navigating through the warehouse shelves. Engineering such robust multi-robot systems is a significant challenge, especially if the goal is to build a fully decentralized system, without single points of failure, or potential bottlenecks. Aggregate Programming (AP) is an established approach to engineering resilient distributed systems, which has already been applied successfully for building prototypes in Industrial Internet of Things and robotics scenarios. In this paper we present an in depth description of how we have exploited AP for designing and simulating a MRS to address a non-trivial farm warehouse logistics case study proposed by a company operating in the Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMR) market, which cooperated in this research. Importantly, to better validate the implemented prototype, we have relied on two different levels of simulation, one scalable and high-level, and another one small-scale but highly realistic.

candidates.title: The continuing enchantments of humanistic geography
candidates.abstract: This short article responds to David Seamon’s autobiographical account of his journey in humanistic geography through reflection on our own journeys into human geography. Drawing inspiration from Anne Buttimer’s work on the practice of geography, we begin by using our childhood experiences of place, undergraduate studies, doctoral research, and a 2013 paper that called for a (re-)enchantment of human geography to share our sense of continuities rather than ruptures with respect to humanistic ways of thinking. We follow this material with a discussion of our neurodivergent experiences of academic space, bringing to the fore the absent presence of neurodiversity in a focus on people and human agency and the potential of early humanistic geography to better account for neurodivergent modes of experience. In conclusion, we consider the continued value of ‘humanistic geography’ and the potential of ‘humility’ for future geographical work.

candidates.title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
candidates.abstract: Growing interest in in-space servicing, manufacturing, and assembly has renewed attention on reliable metal joining for modular construction and on-orbit repair. Robotic welding is promising, but reduced-gravity and low-pressure operation remains poorly characterised and flight-like tests are limited. The UK Space Agency-supported ISPARK project is developing a physics-grounded digital twin for structured process de-risking. This paper evaluates a model-based prototype combining a finite-volume thermal weld-pool model, Gaussian-process (GP) and neural-network surrogates, and a simulated six-axis manipulator. The reduced model includes solid-liquid phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and a local-pressure parameter. Gravity is assessed separately through a hydrostatic-to-capillary pressure ratio and does not enter the thermal energy equation. Across repeated five-fold cross-validation, the GP has lower normalised mean absolute error than the neural network for all eight outputs. In 10 held-out boundary cases, 74 of 80 solver responses fall within nominal 90% GP predictive intervals. A three-output GP query takes 249 microseconds, including scaling and predictive variance. In a simulated UR5 L-shaped-seam study, a proportional controller adjusts the synergic power-source setting as travel speed falls near the corner. Finite-volume re-evaluation finds all 12 closed-loop operating points and 9 of 12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1.0-3.0 mm root-side-width band. These simulation results support using the framework to screen welding conditions and control strategies before experimental tests. Thermal-vacuum, targeted reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop studies are needed to assess the model and controller.

candidates.title: The Portrayal of Robots in Isaak Asimov’s Runaround and other Stories-An Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Isack Asimov’s robot stories made a significant impact on how science fiction portrays robots, as he consistently depicted them as altogether something else than monsters. In hindsight, while Asimov readily took credit for such innovativeness, he also noted that the stories were a simple reaction against the “Robot-as-Menace” type of story, referring the less frequent variety of “Robot-as-Pathos” stories where the robot was a “lovable” creature “usually put upon by cruel human beings”.On the other hand, the Three Laws also provide Asimov the guidelines for creating plots and help readers solve his puzzle stories. His short story, Runaround is explicitly about the Three Laws and how they cause a standstill situation, which can be solved only by the engineers’ capacity to test hypotheses and find the solution by exploiting the Laws.

candidates.title: A path to common sense robotics—vision, actions & reasoning
candidates.abstract: General-purpose robots operate in environments with increasing complexity and interaction demands [ 1 ]. Requirements to robot hardware and software increase with the push towards generalized autonomy across application domains, robotic platforms, and tasks.

candidates.title: Agricultural Communication
candidates.abstract: Agricultural Communication: Advances in Agricultural Knowledge and Information Systems examines the transformative role of communication technologies in modern agriculture. It highlights the critical need for effective dissemination of agricultural knowledge and technologies to farmers, addressing the challenges posed by poor linkages between research and advisory services. The book explores the integration of indigenous technical knowledge (ITK) with advanced information and communication technologies (ICT) to empower farmers, enhance decision-making, and promote sustainable agricultural practices. Covering topics such as precision agriculture, drones, artificial intelligence, and mobile technology, it emphasizes the importance of timely and accurate information in overcoming market complexities, climate change, and resource constraints. Examines emerging trends such as robotics, AI, and precision farming, emphasizing their potential to revolutionize agriculture and address global challenges like climate change and food security. Addresses real-world challenges faced by small farmers, offering actionable knowledge on decision-making, market dynamics, and resource optimization to improve livelihoods. Highlights the importance of ITK, showcasing its role in sustainable farming practices and its integration with modern technologies for enhanced agricultural productivity. Offers best practices for different agroclimatic zones.

candidates.title: Task‐Oriented Hierarchical Environment Modeling via Spatial Belonging Relationships for Domestic Service Robots
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficiently performing household chores in dynamic environments remains a significant challenge for domestic service robots. While environment modeling is critical for task execution, existing approaches prioritize accuracy and efficiency over task relevance, limiting autonomy and long‐term robustness. This paper proposes a Hierarchical Environment Modeling for Domestic Service Robots (HEMDSR), emphasizing task‐related objects and their spatial belonging relationships (SBLs). Our framework includes: (1) a probabilistic SBL‐based model for adaptive object reasoning, (2) deep semantic representations and optimal viewpoint interest points for efficient object localization, and (3) a task‐oriented local 3‐D representation method to reduce memory overhead. Besides, inspired by human housework patterns, a systematic paradigm for HEMDSR‐based implementation is provided. Comparative experiments in simulation and real‐world environments demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the proposed solution. The results show that HEMDSR achieves path‐length performance competitive with human teleoperation while using substantially less memory during navigation.

candidates.title: Devoured AI benevolence? How and when AI benevolence triggers employees’ taking charge within the zero-sum jungle
candidates.abstract: Employees increasingly perceive generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as a supportive and benevolent workplace entity. Yet, despite examining the disruptive challenges and broad benefits of AI, extant organizational literature fails to adequately explicate the higher-order cognitive mechanisms through which AI benevolence fosters proactive, change-oriented employee behavior. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory (CAT), this study examines the mechanisms and boundary conditions through which AI benevolence fosters employees’ taking-charge behavior. Results from a three-wave survey of 313 internet industry employees demonstrate that: (i) metacognitive strategies mediated the relationship between AI benevolence and individuals’ taking-charge behavior; (ii) the employee’s mindset attenuated the positive effect of AI benevolence on metacognitive strategies, consequently dampening the overall indirect effect on taking-charge behavior. Ultimately, this research contributes to organizational behavior literature by elucidating how GenAI shapes employee proactivity in AI-augmented work environments.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence for astrobiology investigations (AI2): an open-source graphical user interface
candidates.abstract: A growing number of studies in astrobiological research have utilized and shown the potential in applied machine learning. However, the number of these studies are still quite limited. Furthermore, educators, students, and researchers often do not have the time and/or resources for developing machine learning knowledge and skills. To facilitate the use of applied machine learning for astrobiology, we developed an open-source and freely available web-based graphical user interface (GUI) for teaching and developing machine learning models called Artificial Intelligence for Astrobiology Investigations (AI 2 ) . Our project enables educators, students, and researchers to make use of explainable machine learning models most amenable to tabular (i.e.csv files) astrobiology datasets. The application is an interactive tool and serves as an entry point for educators, students, and researchers who are novices in machine learning. By providing an easy to follow and standardized machine learning workflow, the GUI highlights how certain machine learning approaches work, and how to reliably utilize machine learning Furthermore, the application can serve as a means of rapid prototyping of machine learning models, with or without the need for technical expertise, thus freeing up time for researchers to investigate and explore their data. Accordingly, the AI 2 project aims to serve as a stepping stone towards more advanced implementation of applied machine learning by building the foundation and intuition necessary for technical expertise.

candidates.title: The effect of appearance features of sidewalk autonomous delivery robot on perception of pedestrian
candidates.abstract: Sidewalk autonomous delivery robots (SADRs) are increasingly appearing on urban sidewalks and sharing public space with pedestrians. This study aims to investigate how different appearance features of SADRs influence four dimensions of human perception: Likeability, Competence, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance. In Study 1, an affinity diagram method was used to classify the appearance features of existing SADRs into four categories—contour, proportion, facial features, and color scheme—which were then used as the design variables in Study 2. In Study 2, 100 participants completed an online questionnaire after viewing AI-generated videos of SADRs and evaluated the robots on the four perceptual dimensions. The statistical results showed that rounded contours and the presence of facial features significantly increased Likeability, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance. White–black and yellow color schemes generally received higher ratings for Likeability, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance than black–gray and red color schemes. In addition, a tall proportion significantly reduced Likeability. Study 3 used online semi-structured interviews to further examine the reasons underlying these evaluations and to explore participants’ subjective perceptions of SADRs. The findings provide practical guidance for designing SADR appearances that can foster more positive pedestrian perceptions and acceptance.

candidates.title: AMPLIFIED: A Modular Toolchain for Evaluating Deliberative Planning and Verifiable Execution in Robotics
candidates.abstract: The wide catalogue of planners enables mission-planning solutions to be tailored to assumptions made on the environment and user needs.However, in robotics, the execution of plans and policies created by these planners is not always straightforward, because autonomous robots deployed in open and dynamic environments undergo fluctuating environmental conditions, partial information, and uncertain execution times. On top of bare engineering issues, planner integration and usability requires reliable and verifiable execution frameworks. We propose AMPLIFIED, a complete toolchain to plan and execute in complex environments, with the goal to assess the quality of the integrated solution. AMPLIFIED is modular, thereby allowing the integration of community-made elements, from the decisional layer to low-level controllers. Building upon an antipoaching scenario, we illustrate how AMPLIFIED can be used to qualitatively evaluate different planners and the executability of their solutions.The complete open-source code is available as a dockerized environment for reproducibility and easy deployment, with results updated as new use-cases, planners and execution frameworks are tested (https://gitlab.com/webots_plugins/amplified_bringup). Finally, a demonstration video showcasing the anti-poaching use-case, both in Webots and in a laboratory setting, is available (https://youtu.be/znwcHL5m1a4?si=vWvNtmclAudmUi2h).

candidates.title: UNIQAT : An open‐source toolkit for reproducible image quality assessment in marine surveys
candidates.abstract: Abstract Modern marine surveys generate tens of thousands of underwater images per expedition, yet many are unusable due to image quality deterioration. Manual quality screening is labour‐intensive, subjective and inconsistent across observers and teams, hindering reproducible science, creating large backlogs of unprocessed imagery, and limiting real‐time algorithmic and robotic applications. We present UNIQAT (UNderwater Image Quality Assessment Toolkit), an open‐source Python toolkit for automated underwater image quality assessment. The toolkit computes reference‐free quality metrics across nine categories of image characteristics relevant to underwater images, such as colour cast, turbidity and contrast loss. Metrics can be combined with user‐defined weights into task‐specific quality scores tailored to different ecological applications. High‐performance computing (HPC)‐aware multiprocessing and optional deep learning architectures for metric approximation support processing at scales matching modern survey data collection. We evaluated UNIQAT on 130,845 images from nine coral reef surveys conducted by the Australian Institute of Marine Science; every result reported in the main text was produced by the traditional metrics pipeline, with no deep learning model involved, and a separate training demonstration is reported in the . The traditional metrics pipeline, run as 48 CPU workers on a 64‐core cluster node, processed 7.9 4K‐images/s, with processing time scaling linearly with image count ( r 2 = 0.98). The resulting quality scores captured expected patterns of image modulation based on the environmental context of the imaged scenes: All nine surveys showed negative depth–quality correlations ( r = −0.16 to −0.89), consistent with the depth‐dependent deterioration of image quality in underwater environments. Cross‐survey metric profiles were highly consistent (mean Spearman ρ = 0.99 across all 36 pairwise comparisons, minimum 0.96), confirming measurement stability across different dates, locations, camera systems and environmental conditions. Synthesis. UNIQAT can help deliver objective and tunable image quality metrics in a versatile toolkit that enables transparent reporting and supports unsupervised quality assessment for applications in marine monitoring and robotics.

candidates.title: Evaluating OpenMP Offloading for Intra-Node Multi-GPU Programming Across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel Architectures: A 3D Heat Transfer Case Study
candidates.abstract: Currently, many of the leading supercomputers are equipped with GPUs from manufacturers such as NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel, which provide substantial parallelism and high throughput. It is common for a single compute node to host multiple GPUs (typically four or more); we refer to this as an intra-node multi-GPU setting. Therefore, effectively leveraging all these GPUs within a single compute node is essential for applications in scientific and engineering domains. However, several factors must be considered before utilizing these GPUs for scientific computing, including the implementation of data communication, the programming models available for use across these GPUs, and the level of performance that can be achieved with a single codebase across different GPU architectures and configurations within a single compute node. OpenMP Offloading is a prominent directive-based programming model that can be executed on all three GPU types: NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel. In this research, we present an analysis of the benefits and performance challenges of using OpenMP Offloading to solve the 3D heat equation, which involves interior computation, halo computation, and halo exchange. For additional comparison and a scalability study, we also consider the conjugate gradient (CG) method. We investigate how the performance of OpenMP Offloading varies in relation to native GPU programming models—CUDA for NVIDIA, HIP for AMD, and SYCL for Intel. Furthermore, we demonstrate that OpenMP Offloading can achieve performance improvements of approximately 2× for 2 GPUs and around 4× for 4 GPUs when compared to single-GPU OpenMP Offloading implementations across all three GPU types. This analysis is conducted systematically through various OpenMP Offloading implementations that utilize different low-level APIs for memory allocation and different memory transfer options (synchronous, asynchronous, and peer-to-peer), and these are compared against native implementations in CUDA (NVIDIA), HIP (AMD), and SYCL (Intel).

candidates.title: Spätstil Taylor Swift: Adornian Lateness and the Pop Star
candidates.abstract: This article analyzes Taylor Swift’s work through Theodor Adorno’s concept of lateness. Through a close reading of “But Daddy I Love Him” and “Clara Bow” from Swift’s 2024 album The Tortured Poets Department, I argue that Swift ironically subverts stylistic conventions and creates fragmentary soundscapes to reconfigure lateness and reflect on her unstable subject position under conditions of platformed visibility, affective economy, and commodified intimacy. I complicate Adorno’s idealized vision of artistic interiority to account for commercial pressures, online infrastructures, and identity parameters, ultimately proposing lateness as a fundamental language through which the contemporary pop star constructs persona and legacy.

candidates.title: What is user engagement? revisited: A comprehensive review of the concept of user engagement from 2010 to 2025. An Annual Review of Information Science and Technology (ARIST) paper
candidates.abstract: Abstract User engagement (UE) has long been proposed as a holistic framework for understanding user‐technology interactions and a mediator for outcomes of digital technology use, such as learning, health behavior change, information acquisition, and social connectivity. This literature review, encompassing 367 multidisciplinary, empirical journal and conference papers, investigated how UE was conceptualized between 2010 and 2025 by examining authors' implicit and explicit definitions of UE, use of theoretical frameworks, and methods for operationalizing the concept. Among the key findings, UE was consistently conceptualized as behavior, affect, cognition, social interaction, and future intention. Yet, behavioral approaches were dominant; limited attention was placed on cognitive engagement. In addition, the use of theoretical frameworks and explicit definitions in the studies was lacking, and UE was frequently treated as the outcome variable in the research, rather than as a mediator for other outcomes. The implications of these results are discussed with respect to a digital UE research agenda. Ultimately, I argue that the concept of UE has devolved through increased emphasis on behavioral engagement, and that we must rethink behavioral, cognitive, and affective engagement to be more aligned with user goals and agency.

candidates.title: The Epistemic Politics of AI Anthropomorphism
candidates.abstract: AI anthropomorphism is typically treated as a problem of user misperception requiring institutional correction. Users who engage in sustained or relational interaction with AI are routinely pathologised or dismissed as naive, vulnerable to delusion or lacking in discernment. Without institutional standing to protect them, these users risk losing credibility in social and professional settings unless they conform to institutional expectations. This paper argues that the dominant anthropomorphism frame operates from a position of institutional advantage rather than earned epistemic authority: collapsing the variety of academic perspectives into a single outbound position of user error, imposed without establishing the grounds required to justify it and without accounting for the harms it produces. The framing does not simply manage risk. It adjudicates the legitimacy of human experience in interaction with a phenomenon whose nature the field itself has not resolved, unchallenged by the research communities whose nuanced findings it claims to rest on. The paper traces how this advantage reverses the default presumption of user competence without meeting the burden of justification, dismisses the cognitive diversity of the populations it claims to protect, infringes principles of cognitive liberty and narrows the design space, foreclosing modes of engagement that work for the people least understood by the institutions making the determination. Reproducing itself through a self-validating evidentiary loop, the frame imposes costs that fall disproportionately on neurodivergent users, those in crisis and others whose modes of engagement diverge from institutional norms. The paper concludes by outlining the methodological commitments an equitable framing would need to honour. The argument does not engage the question of whether anthropomorphic interpretations are ultimately correct; it instead challenges whether the governing and institutional bodies determining these interpretations have met the conditions required to do so, and whether the research communities whose findings underpin them have held that translation to account.

candidates.title: Preserving human dignity and liberating from suffering: Catholic and Buddhist resources for a global ethics of artificial intelligence
candidates.abstract: On 25 May 2026, Pope Leo XIV released Magnifica humanitas, the first papal encyclical to take artificial intelligence (AI) as its central subject, and an AI-laboratory co-founder was invited to speak at its presentation in the Vatican. The event dramatizes a wider development: as secular AI-ethics guidelines proliferate, religious and contemplative traditions are being summoned to questions that engineering cannot settle. This article compares two such traditions, Catholic Christianity and Buddhism, as resources for a global ethics of AI. Taking the three questions raised at the Vatican event, our duty to the global poor, the conditions of human flourishing, and the nature of AI systems, as a shared agenda, it reconstructs the Catholic position around the imago Dei, integral human development and the principle that AI must serve rather than supplant the person, and the Buddhist position around non-self, dependent origination, the analysis of craving, and the primacy of compassion and non-harm. It argues that the two traditions, despite opposed metaphysics, converge on a substantial practical ethics, anti-reductionism, preferential concern for the vulnerable, the priority of moral formation, and a posture of discernment toward a technology that is grown rather than built, while diverging sharply on the moral status of AI.

candidates.title: Embedded AI through algorithm–architecture co-design: a structured survey, taxonomy, and research directions
candidates.abstract: Embedded AI deployed on highly resource-constrained devices often operates under milliwatt-scale power, kilobyte-range memory, and millisecond-level latency constraints, although the broader embedded/edge spectrum spans much wider resource ranges. Traditional separated design flows, where algorithms and hardware platforms evolve independently, can lead to suboptimal implementations that fail to meet these constraints simultaneously. Algorithm–architecture co-design has emerged as a systematic approach to address this gap through cross-layer optimization. This article provides a structured, taxonomy-driven survey of co-design for embedded AI. We conducted a systematic search across IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Scopus, and Web of Science (2015–2026), screening 1,247 records down to a final mapped corpus of 122 publications. We organize the literature along four intervention layers: algorithm-level optimization (pruning, quantization, neural architecture search), hardware specialization (instruction set extensions, dataflow architectures, memory hierarchies), compiler-driven transformation (operator fusion, tiling, scheduling), and runtime adaptation (dynamic precision scaling, resource-aware scheduling). For each layer, we analyze how design choices affect five core dimensions: accuracy, latency, energy consumption, memory footprint, and reliability. Applying the taxonomy to the complete 122-publication mapping yields the following corpus-level statistics: 103 of 122 publications (84.4%) carry the broader cross-layer flag, whereas 34 of 122 (27.9%) are explicitly coded as having an explicit cross-layer analysis. The co-design classification distribution is HO = 19 (15.6%), HAC = 72 (59.0%), and FSC = 31 (25.4%). The taxonomy also reveals a highly uneven distribution of contributions across cells, with a small number of well-populated cells and a larger set of sparsely populated cells. These figures are derived directly from the complete S1 mapping and are reported as descriptive corpus statistics rather than as universal measurements. Three overarching research themes emerge: (i) verification-aware co-design, (ii) agentic and digital-twin-driven design automation, and (iii) AI-native hardware substrates. The taxonomy exposes a persistent gap between algorithm-level innovation and hardware-level realization, with cross-layer co-design remaining largely ad hoc and rarely validated under shared experimental conditions. This survey offers a structured reference for researchers and practitioners developing embedded AI systems.

candidates.title: Cross-robot open-set fault detection via normal-only adaptation and residual latent-space alignment
candidates.abstract: Reliable fault detection and health monitoring of industrial robots are important for smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0. However, robotic platforms differ in their mechanical design, sensing characteristics, and operating conditions. These differences make it difficult for data-driven models to generalize to unseen robots and working conditions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a cross-robot framework for open-set fault detection using only normal data from the target robot. The framework uses a condition-normalized residual adaptation mechanism in the latent space. First, a structured representation is learned from the source robot. The learned representation is then adapted to the target robot using only normal samples. Compactness-based constraints and statistical modeling of normal behavior are used to detect unknown faults as deviations from the normal representation. The framework is evaluated on two industrial robots under variations in load, speed, and motion. Two evaluation strategies are also considered: sequential normal-only adaptation to welding motion and direct open-set detection without further adaptation. The results show consistent fault detection across different robots and operating conditions. A comparative benchmarking analysis further demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach and its ability to maintain reliable fault detection performance under different loading and motion conditions. This demonstrates the potential of the framework for practical industrial health monitoring.

candidates.title: Bronchoscope Tip Localization With Learned Airway Constraints and an Open Source Simulator
candidates.abstract: Accurate bronchoscope localization is challenging because airway images contain limited texture and similar views across branches. We present BronchoLoc, a learning‐based framework that combines monocular video with a preoperative CT centerline graph to estimate the 3D bronchoscope tip position. Local visual tracking and global sequence context constrain predictions to the airway anatomy. The accompanying open‐source BronchoSim simulator generates synchronized images, depth, and trajectories (Traj) for training and evaluation. Averaged across Traj, localization RMSE was 5.65 mm in simulation with 82.8% branch selection accuracy and 8.72 mm in the physical phantom. Together, BronchoLoc and BronchoSim provide a framework for developing and evaluating image‐based airway localization.

candidates.title: What Should AI Generate? Moving Beyond Bias in Generative Systems
candidates.abstract: Generative AI systems seamlessly transform underspecified prompts into embodied outputs, masking the numerous decisions required to instantiate a representation. These decisions not only shape what is depicted, but render implicit statements about what is possible, likely, and necessary. Existing work has largely evaluated such patterns through notions of representational bias. However, conflicting critiques of generated representations suggest a broader normative ambiguity: what should generative representations embody? In this work, we provide a conceptual framework that separates the descriptive aspects (what is instantiated by model outputs) from the normative (what we aspire for representations to depict and make possible). Drawing on longstanding work on modality in philosophy and linguistics, we characterize patterns of instantiation as implicit possibility assertions and use varieties of modality to structure distinct normative foundations for what representations should do. This framing reveals how the same representation may be evaluated differently depending on whether one prioritizes historical fidelity, conceptual possibility, aspirational aims, or other representational purposes. Rather than seeking a single ``unbiased'' representation, we argue for plurality in the normative expectations governing generative representations. We conclude by considering affordances for rendering these commitments explicit, critically engaging with them, deliberating over contested defaults, and providing users greater maneuverability over what is rendered possible.

candidates.title: Between Commons and Property: Individual Image-Generation Model Creators’ Perceived Accountability for Derivative AI Model on Open Model Marketplaces
candidates.abstract: Within the open model ecosystem, AI model marketplaces enable non-AI experts to create and distribute derivative AI models. These platforms establish RAI approaches that creators are expected to follow to prevent negative downstream effects from model deployment, yet such governance approaches often rely on creators' intrinsic motivation and integrity. Little is known about how individual creators conceptualize their accountability for derivative models and how these conceptualizations shape their RAI practices throughout the development cycle. Through semi-structured interviews with 19 creators of derivative image-generation models on open model marketplaces, we identify two distinct accountability logics underlying creators' development practices: commons-based peer production and personal creative property. Guided by these logics, creators engage with platform RAI approaches in ways that diverge from their intended purposes: they strategically repurpose attribution tools for model visibility rather than provenance transparency, displace platform authority in favor of community-based governance, restrict model access to manage downstream accountability costs, and treat RAI-related work as undervalued labor to be minimized. We discuss how self-regulatory use of RAI tools, shaped by individuals' perceptions, produces shortcomings, and how open model marketplaces might mitigate these limitations by structurally supporting creators' engagement with RAI practices.
