candidates.title: A deep hybrid feature extraction model based on MobileNet and vision transformer for acute lymphoblastic leukemia prediction
candidates.abstract: Abstract Early and accurate identification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from peripheral blood smear images can support microscopic screening, but reliable evaluation requires both discriminative feature learning and transparent reporting of the experimental protocol. This study presents MoViTHAFX-Net, a hybrid MobileNet–Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture with Hierarchical Attention Fusion (HAF) and Grad-CAM++ visualization for binary classification of ALL blasts and healthy hematogones (HEM) using the 10,661 labelled cell images in the training component of the C-NMC 2019 dataset. MobileNet extracts local morphological information, whereas ViT models long-range contextual relationships. HAF first refines the two branches and then adaptively combines three learnable morphology-guided feature projections before binary classification. The reported experiment uses an image-level stratified partition containing 7462 training images, 1600 validation images, and 1599 held-out test images; augmentation is restricted to the training partition. On the held-out test partition, the model correctly classified 1583 of 1599 images, corresponding to 99.00% accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-score of approximately 0.990 and an AUC of 0.99. Ablation results within the same experimental setting indicate an incremental advantage of HAF over direct CNN–ViT concatenation. Grad-CAM++ is used as a qualitative post hoc visualization of image regions contributing to predictions. Because the reported custom split is image-level rather than subject-disjoint and evaluation is limited to a single benchmark dataset, the results should be interpreted as internal benchmark performance rather than evidence of patient-independent or multicentre clinical generalization.

candidates.title: openCFS: An open-source finite-element software for advanced multiphysics simulations
candidates.abstract: The software openCFS (formerly “CFS + + ”) is an open-source finite-element software designed for coupled field simulations including electromagnetics, acoustics, linearized fluid flow, solid mechanics, and heat transfer. It combines a modular C + + core with a declarative XML modeling language and a Python automation layer (pyCFS). Besides standard formulations, openCFS provides advanced capabilities such as time-domain equivalent-fluid modeling for dispersive porous materials, thermoviscous/viscous acoustics with Maxwell slip boundary conditions on moving domains, advanced vector hysteresis models in electromagnetics, and robust treatment of non-conforming and rotating interfaces, complemented by density-based and feature-mapping topology optimization. Development follows modern software-engineering practice, with continuous integration and more than 600 automated tests across platforms. This article describes the architecture, workflow, and key features, and demonstrates them on representative applications.

candidates.title: Future of Anticipatory Robotics in Manufacturing
candidates.abstract: Collaborative robots, designed to work alongside humans in shared environments, are transforming manufacturing production lines, enabling partial automation and boosting productivity. But their potential extends beyond these benefits. By implementing anticipatory strategies to prevent workers’ risky behaviours and reduce excessive workloads, collaborative robots can proactively enhance working conditions. For example, they can take on repetitive or strenuous tasks to reduce physical effort or adjust the pace of operations to help alleviate stress levels. Indeed, Musculoskeletal Disorders (MSDs) and Common Mental Disorders (CMDs), which arise from uncontrolled physical and cognitive loads, are major work-related health problems in developed countries, with incommensurate social and economic costs. Collaborative robots can curb the effect of such disorders and help in preserving workers’ health. This Chapter addresses how Human Factors and Ergonomics (HFE) can be monitored to provide robots with relevant inputs about the human state, and how robots can be employed to improve HFE. Novel strategies are proposed to adapt online robot behaviour to the workers’ psycho-physical state and enhance their well-being and productivity.

candidates.title: Design and development of IoT based solar power agriculture robot
candidates.abstract: Agriculture in developing economies such as Pakistan remains heavily dependent on manual labor and single-purpose, grid or fuel-powered machinery that is often unaffordable for smallholder farmers. This paper presents the design, fabrication, and experimental evaluation of a multifunctional, solar-powered, Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled agricultural robot capable of performing soil cultivation, seed placement, irrigation, and crop cutting within a single integrated platform. The system architecture is built around an ESP32 microcontroller that interfaces with a DHT11 temperature/humidity sensor, an HC-SR04 ultrasonic obstacle sensor, an ESP32-CAM module for visual field monitoring, an L298N dual H-bridge motor driver, and relay-controlled actuators, with energy supplied by a 20 W photovoltaic panel, a 12 V/7.2 Ah battery, and a battery management system (BMS). Mechanical subsystems comprising a tooth-type cultivator, a soil-leveling roller, a servo-actuated seed dispenser, a DC pump-based irrigation unit, and a blade-type cutter were designed in CAD, fabricated, and integrated onto a four-wheel-drive chassis. Engineering calculations were used to size the power budget, battery backup, drive-motor torque, structural factor of safety, seeding rate, and irrigation flow. Field trials show a typical operating power demand of 24.4 W against an average usable solar output of 11–12 W, a battery backup of approximately 3.5 h, The experimental results demonstrated satisfactory performance of the proposed agricultural robot, achieving an average seed-placement accuracy of 74.45% over 11 experimental trials. The developed system also successfully performed soil digging, irrigation, crop cutting, obstacle detection, and real-time IoT-based remote monitoring, demonstrating its suitability for sustainable precision agriculture.

candidates.title: Field Notes from a Low-Cost Robot Learning Lab: Hardware Churn, Software Whiplash, and What Actually Went Wrong
candidates.abstract: This is the informal companion to two more rigorous papers from the same project. Over roughly seven weeks we trained imitation-learning policies on a self-built SO-101 robot arm, and along the way we moved the work between machines more often than planned, rebuilt the camera setup, fought a fast-moving open-source framework, and lost an embarrassing amount of time to causes that turned out to be a loose power cable, a swapped port, or a missing audio package. The quantified findings are reported elsewhere. Here we tell the rest: what the hardware and software path actually looked like, which incidents cost us the most time and why, what we would warn a newcomer about, and which threads we deliberately left unfinished. We write for people building something similar on a hobbyist budget, not for reviewers, and we try to be as candid about our mistakes as about our results.

candidates.title: Occupational Wearable Robotics
candidates.abstract: Injuries and occupational diseases represent an important economic factor in different industrial sectors. In Italy alone, there have been over 60000 confirmed cases of occupational diseases in 2022, where musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) represent 70% of the total. This fact highlights the importance of protecting workers against physical efforts. While current ergonomic tools can mitigate most of the risk factors, there is still a non-negligible number of tasks that cannot be completely compensated for. This is due to the high complexity and costs of the workplace reorganization, or simply strict requirements of the target task. In some of these cases, exoskeletons are a viable solution. This chapter introduces different kinds of existing exoskeletons, with particular focus on occupational exoskeletons, considering commercial systems already deployed in industry, and some of the most promising technologies which will arrive in the next years. The deployment of occupational exoskeletons is conditioned by the regulatory frameworks and by the required reorganization of the workplace. Both concepts and the latest developments are discussed in this chapter, including their integration into Industry 4.0. Finally, this chapter describes the most common evaluation methods and discusses current efforts toward standardized benchmarking methods which will allow evaluating the benefit of using exoskeletons in real applications.

candidates.title: Shared Control for Assistive and Collaborative Robotics
candidates.abstract: Assistive and collaborative robots offer a promising solution for reducing human physical stress and exposure across a broad range of applications. The design and control of such robotic systems should account for humans needs, so as to assist their motion and activity as well as optimize their efficiency and performance throughout the considered tasks. In this respect, designing around the human means accounting for their musculoskeletal constraints, features, and limitations during the development of robotic mechanical systems and control algorithms, such as powered exoskeletons or cobots. This Chapter presents an overview of human-centered design and shared control techniques in robotics, including supporting examples and applications in the field of industrial teleoperation and mobility assistance. We also discuss the perspectives of the field and how such human-centered approaches can be beneficial to a broader range of applications than those where it is implemented nowadays.

candidates.title: Blockchain Security: An Empirical Evaluation of High‐Impact Exploits and Detection Tools
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Blockchain introduced secure, peer‐to‐peer transactions in decentralized environments without reliance on central authorities. However, attackers continue to exploit blockchain projects. Over the past decade, reported blockchain exploit losses have exceeded $24 billion. Although existing research analyzes blockchain vulnerabilities and real‐world incidents, many studies focus on specific vulnerability classes or smart contract issues only. Therefore, we present an empirical study of major blockchain exploits from 2020 to 2025. Based on detailed analysis of these exploits, we introduce a practitioner‐oriented taxonomy that organizes the dominant root causes observed in the analyzed exploits across four domains: Human Risks, Off‐Chain Infrastructure Vulnerabilities, Private Key Compromises, and Smart Contract Vulnerabilities. Across these categories, we present case studies, code illustrations where applicable, and mitigation strategies. Moreover, we evaluate five vulnerability‐detection tools spanning four paradigms, namely static analysis ( Slither , 4naly3er ), symbolic execution ( Mythril ), bounded/formal verification ( SMTChecker ), and LLM‐assisted analysis ( GPTScan ), on a curated test suite of vulnerable and secure contracts. Our results show detection gaps under the evaluated setting: Slither, Mythril, and 4naly3er all scored recall below 40%. SMTChecker and GPTScan were evaluated separately because of their narrower target scopes. SMTChecker detected only arithmetic issues, while GPTScan produced no benchmark‐relevant detections. The study highlights the high average loss associated with smart contract access‐control failures, the need for post‐deployment monitoring beyond one‐time audits, and risks related to Off‐Chain Infrastructure Vulnerabilities. By analyzing exploits and offering mitigations, we provide a structured reference for identifying, prioritizing, and mitigating major blockchain security risks.

candidates.title: AI Companions and Loneliness: Conceptualizing and Operationalizing Synthetic Mindfulness and Exploring Its Role in Alleviating Loneliness
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The rise of AI companions has sparked interest in their potential to alleviate the growing social problem of loneliness, yet evidence of their effectiveness remains unsettled. Drawing on social surrogacy theory with a theories‐in‐use approach, this research introduces synthetic mindfulness, defined as consumers' judgment of an AI companion's capacity to maintain an attentive presence, engage in a non‐judgmental way, and respond with sensitive attunement to their needs. We argue that these judgments shape whether consumers experience AI companions as capable of reducing their loneliness. Across one qualitative and four quantitative studies, we develop and validate a three‐dimensional measure of synthetic mindfulness. Our final study demonstrates that higher judgments of synthetic mindfulness reduce loneliness via consumers' strengthened sense of belonging and self‐esteem. This research advances understanding of how AI companions can effectively address loneliness and provides a conceptual foundation for examining synthetic mindfulness in human–AI relationships.

candidates.title: SPREAD, a framework and open-source R toolbox to quantify behavioural contagion
candidates.abstract: Behavioural contagion, when one individual's behaviour increases the likelihood of similar behaviours in others, is a fundamental dimension of social interaction, yet its empirical quantification remains methodologically challenging. Distinguishing contagion from coincidental co-occurrence, resolving contagion across continuous latencies rather than within fixed windows, accounting for behavioural base rates, and incorporating social structure require integrated analytical solutions. We present SPREAD, a conceptual and statistical framework implemented as an open-source R toolbox for quantifying behavioural contagion in time-series interaction data. SPREAD compares observed behavioural sequences with null distributions generated from permuted data that preserve individual event frequencies while disrupting inter-individual temporal alignment. The framework yields latency-resolved, base-rate corrected estimates of contagion strength that are comparable across behaviours and social configurations. We demonstrate SPREAD across two behavioural domains, laughter and eating, using human triadic data and illustrate its ability to detect contagion effects across distinct temporal dynamics.

candidates.title: Ritual Paraphernalia Toward a Modular Approach to Coptic Magic
candidates.abstract: This article explores the redactional strategies through which ritual experts in late antique and early medieval Egypt articulated their textual products. It adopts what is here heuristically termed a ‘modular approach’, which treats magical texts as assemblages of discrete textual segments that could be extracted, recombined, and adapted to different redactional agendas. Drawing on selected case studies from Coptic ritual manuscripts, the article offers a new model for understanding scribal practice and the transmission of ritual knowledge.

candidates.title: Smartphone Communities
candidates.abstract: Smartphone Communities places the smartphone - our most personal and ubiquitous medium - at the centre of an in-depth exploration of contemporary community formation. The book ground-breaking contribution lies in theorizing the smartphone not merely as a device, but as a dynamic social infrastructure through which communities are continuously assembled, negotiated, and contested. Conceptualizing the smartphone user as a mobile, permanently networked subject, the book advances a multi-directional media-theoretical framework that bridges participation theory, fan studies, and visual culture. Focusing primarily on Western, platform-capitalist contexts from the 2010s to the mid-2020s, Anne Ganzert analyzes topical and widely recognizable case studies, including TikTok, Pokémon Go, Tinder, and Habitica. These platforms serve as lenses through which social, economic, and political power relations become visible, from algorithmic governance and data extraction to practices of play, intimacy, self-optimization, and resistance. Readers will gain a comprehensive understanding of smartphone-based communities through a blend of media theory and empirical analysis. Addressed to undergraduates, postgraduates, scholars of media and cultural studies, as well as non-specialist readers such as librarians and booksellers, the book offers an accessible yet theoretically ambitious account of smartphone-based communities.

candidates.title: Developing and validating the attitudes toward large language models scale
candidates.abstract: With large language models (LLMs) now embedded in a wide range of everyday technologies, there is increasing interest in accurately measuring public attitudes toward these systems. General AI attitude instruments may not fully capture attitudes specific to LLMs. To address this gap, we adapted the 5-item Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence (ATAI) scale, a dual-component scale measuring AI Fear and AI Acceptance, and developed two new measures: the Attitudes Toward General LLMs (AT-GLLM) and Attitudes Toward Primary LLM (AT-PLLM) scales, assessing general attitudes and attitudes toward the LLM each respondent uses most. Both instruments were designed specifically for the LLM context and validated in a UK sample of 526 adults (ages 18-45). Psychometric analyses supported a two-factor structure, strong measurement invariance across gender, and acceptable internal consistency across the four subscales (Cronbach’s α = 0.742–0.786; McDonald’s ω = 0.747–0.793). Both scales demonstrated convergent and discriminant validity. These measures offer more precise tools for assessing attitudes toward LLMs than general AI attitude scales and can be used in research and applied settings, enhancing evaluations of user experience and supporting the monitoring of public engagement with this evolving technology.

candidates.title: Intelligent Mechatronics: intelligence in the design process, not only the machine
candidates.abstract: Designing a physical machine requires mechanical, electronic, control, and software decisions to be settled together, each constraining the others, under the standards governing the environment it will work in. This reasoning is held by experienced engineers and rarely written down. That, I argue, is why artificial intelligence has reached the design of software but not of the machines that software runs on. Physical design is, in part, genuinely harder, and its errors are costly and irreversible, but that is not the whole explanation. Software’s design reasoning was written down alongside the public code that an AI could learn from; the knowledge that conceives and sizes a physical system was not. As the design bottleneck shifts to physical systems, intelligence must be applied to the design process itself, not only to the product. Taking mechatronics as the case, I find that where its defining sources invoke intelligence at all, it is for the product or the discipline that builds it, never for the process that designs it. The capture of tacit, cross-domain design knowledge in a form that AI can use is a binding constraint on AI-assisted physical design, and the most neglected as well. A three-layer model locates it: Layer 1, this design knowledge is the missing foundation; the AI reasoning and agent layers above advance rapidly but cannot design physical systems without it. The physical machine and its intelligent twin are developed together from this foundation. A worked design-rationale analysis of an offshore-crane actuation decision grounds what Layer 1 must hold: the rationale residue that existing formats do not capture. In this article, I set out a research agenda, from capturing this knowledge to generalizing beyond mechatronics, and state the conditions under which its central claim would fail.

candidates.title: Steel robots and space turtleships: the divergence of Korean animation and Japanese anime
candidates.abstract: During the Park Chung-hee military dictatorship, Korea shadowed Japanese industrial upgrading at every stage. The same was true in animation, in which Korea took Japanese animations, indigenized them, and imbued them with a techno-nationalism that positioned Korean animation as both dependent on Japan and destined to overcome it. Instead, the opposite happened: today South Korean animation is a pale shadow of Japanese anime’s global success. This essay argues that this divergence, rather than the result of flawed state policies or overdependence on outsourcing, is the result of objective shifts in global capitalism that began in the 1970s. This essay analyses two Korean animated films that mimicked Japanese animated works: Robot Taekwon V (1976), which mimicked Japanese animated film Mazinger Z (1972) and Fly! Spaceship Geobukseon (1979), which mimicked TV series and film Space Battleship Yamato (1974–1975; 1977). While the former Japan-Korea couplet was situated in convergence between the HCI (heavy and chemical industry) economic plans of Japan and Korea, the latter couplet marked the divergence between Korean animation and Japanese ‘anime,’ i.e. the rise of a new commodity form constituted by global ‘otaku’ consumption that reshaped the global economy and ended the previous period’s possibility of economic development.

candidates.title: The Soft Circuits Toolkit: Teaching Mechano-Fluidic Logic for Soft Robotics
candidates.abstract: As soft robotics gains popularity, novel toolkits and educational systems for soft robotics are emerging. These endeavors focus mainly on teaching the programming or fabrication of soft robots, actuators, and sensors. However, as soft robotics moves toward electronics- and software-free control, it becomes essential to gain hands-on experience in soft fluidic circuit building and physical control. We bridge this gap in the educational landscape through the Soft Circuits Toolkit, a modular system of completely soft components that enables the creation and teaching of fluidic circuits, representing fluidic analogies of components such as resistors, capacitors, diodes, and transistors. The toolkit went through two design iterations and four user tests, which ultimately resulted in the toolkit presented in this article, consisting of 17 component types, a manual, and a companion website. User testing across various dimensions, including user experience, with technical university students ( N = 25) indicates that our toolkit is engaging, easy to learn, and promotes problem-solving behaviors. Based on these results, we believe that our kit can support technical universities in teaching about fluidic circuit building and physical control of soft robotics. All fabrication files for this toolkit have been made available open source.

candidates.title: Algorithmic allure: a theoretical framework for dark AI patterns and the erosion of informed consent in AI-driven digital marketing
candidates.abstract: This study examines how generative AI is reshaping digital marketing by enabling unprecedented levels of personalization, automation, and consumer interaction, while simultaneously producing subtler, more complex forms of algorithmic manipulation that extend well beyond conventional dark patterns and threaten meaningful informed consent. Prior research has treated AI-enabled persuasion in a fragmented way—focusing on personalization, recommender systems, or deceptive interface designs in isolation—without offering an integrated account of how generative AI shapes influence across the consumer journey. To address this gap, we conduct a multi-case qualitative analysis of seven documented international incidents of AI-driven marketing practices from 2024 to 2026. Data sources include regulatory reports, investigative journalism, corporate disclosures, and peer-reviewed literature. Using reflexive thematic analysis, we identified seven high-level themes: identity manipulation, social-proof exploitation, synthetic evidence, AI-washing, agentic AI manipulation, synthetic authenticity, and autonomous commercial manipulation. These themes form a taxonomy of “Dark AI Patterns”. Building on these findings, we propose Algorithmic Allure Theory (AAT), which conceptualizes AI-enabled persuasion as a dynamic, six-stage process: observation, interpretation, algorithmic allure, behavioral steering, delegation, and algorithmic governance. AAT argues that contemporary commercial persuasion relies on adaptive computational systems that continuously generate, test, and refine influence tactics in real time—processes that often erode informed consent while preserving a veneer of legitimacy and transparency. Contributions (1) establish Dark AI Patterns as a distinct class of deceptive practices; (2) introduce AAT as a transdisciplinary framework for understanding AI-mediated influence; (3) reconceptualize informed consent as an ongoing cognitive and temporal process rather than a one-time legal event; (4) offer a practical taxonomy to guide future research, regulation, and ethical AI marketing practices As a primary goal.

candidates.title: Toward Mechanical Intelligence in Robotics
candidates.abstract: Conventional robotic systems concentrate sensing, control, and actuation in electronic hardware, creating constraints in harsh environments, energy efficiency, and miniaturization. The physical body of a robot is more than a passive executor of control commands; it is an active substrate that transforms inputs into functional operations through its intrinsic mechanical dynamics. This perspective describes this capability as mechanical intelligence and identifies three core operations: filtering, routing, and switching. These operations address three fundamental questions in physically mediated transformation: what inputs are selectively admitted, where signals propagate, and when the system transitions between states. Together, they enable selective responsiveness, spatial coordination, and state‐dependent behavior without dedicated electronic hardware. Design variables and quantitative metrics are proposed for each operation, and the framework is illustrated in locomotion and manipulation, providing guidance for designing mechanically intelligent robots. Responsive materials extend this framework by transducing environmental stimuli into mechanical signals while also harvesting ambient energy for actuation. Rather than replacing digital computation, mechanical intelligence complements it by embedding part of sensing, processing, and actuation into the physical body, pointing toward hybrid systems in which mechanical and digital intelligence work together.

candidates.title: Transmedia Storytelling
candidates.abstract: Transmedia Storytelling examines how successful stories move between platforms, from traditional media to digital formats, and diagnoses how platform capitalism has transformed transmedia storytelling from a democratic expansion of storyworlds into a machinery of extraction. Drawing on the author’s dual expertise as both producer and academic, this book analyses how storytellers create worlds that work successfully across multiple formats through an abundance of case studies. These case studies span from Marvel and Stranger Things to diverse global storytelling ecologies, including Japanese manga serialisation, Korean platform co-productions, and Nollywood video-film networks. Readers will discover practical tools for developing cross-platform stories, methods for creating effective story bibles and world-building, techniques for adapting characters across different media, and approaches to inclusive storytelling that acknowledge coherence as labour. The book also confronts emerging challenges, including algorithmic personalisation that fragments audiences into parallel monocultures, IP financialisation that transforms franchises into liquid assets, and generative AI that automates the appearance of coherence while degrading narrative causality. This book provides essential reading for undergraduate and postgraduate students undertaking digital storytelling, narrative theory, and film and media production, as well as media studies classes. It also functions as a hands-on toolkit for industry professionals already working within film, gaming, and content creation.

candidates.title: Comparing language models and machine learning classifiers for detecting humorous vaccine misinformation on social media
candidates.abstract: Abstract Misinformation embedded in humor on social media can be difficult to detect and mitigate. This study investigates the effectiveness of traditional machine learning (ML) models, pre-trained neural language models, and large language models (LLMs) in identifying humor-laden misinformation related to COVID-19 vaccines on Twitter. A dataset of 1,500 tweets was randomly sampled from a corpus of 17,945 humorous vaccination disclosures, with human coders annotating the presence of misinformation. We compared logistic regression, a linear support vector classifier (SVC), RoBERTa, and OpenAI’s GPT-4o with a zero-shot and a few-shot prompt, together with a keyword baseline. The few-shot GPT-4o prompt had the highest mean recall and F1 score for the types of misinformation indicated in the prompt and had higher recall and F1 than a keyword baseline built from those same terms. RoBERTa’s accuracy, precision, and F1 score did not differ significantly from GPT-4o’s, and its performance changed little with smaller training sets. Logistic regression and SVC showed lower accuracy, recall, and F1 scores than RoBERTa and the few-shot GPT-4o prompt. This study underscores the potential of LLMs to augment human efforts in detecting complex forms of misinformation on social media and highlights the importance of model selection based on task requirements.

candidates.title: Beyond LLMs: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Commonsense Reasoning in Robotics
candidates.abstract: Domestic robots often receive instructions that are underspecified regarding everyday actions. Large language models can interpret varied language and draw on everyday knowledge, but their reasoning is not explicitly inspectable. Symbolic systems provide transparent knowledge representation and inference, but depend on potentially incomplete rules. This thesis investigates whether combining these approaches can preserve or improve LLM performance on embodied commonsense tasks while making decisions more interpretable. Two complementary neuro-symbolic pipelines are evaluated on RoboCSKBench, a benchmark covering five embodied commonsense tasks. Pipeline 1 investigates the partially automated construction of Answer Set Programming rules for the Tidy Up and Tool Usage tasks, combining commonsense graphs, SOMA-inspired annotations, LLM-generated rule proposals, and Clingo verification. Pipeline 2 covers all five tasks: an LLM extracts controlled facts at runtime, while SWI-Prolog performs reasoning using knowledge-base evidence or hand-crafted rules. Pure-LLM and pure-logic ablations are evaluated using three Mistral model sizes, and Pipeline 2 is transferred without modification to five out-of-distribution datasets. Results show that symbolic reasoning is beneficial only under specific conditions. It is most effective when symbolic components can retrieve relevant affordance or capability knowledge and apply constraints aligned with the task’s answer format. In such cases, explicit grounding can reduce the performance gap between larger and smaller language models. Conversely, for open-ended generation or tasks whose expected decision structure is not supported by the symbolic selector, the architecture may become redundant or harmful. Overall, the findings support a conditional view of neuro-symbolic reasoning: it can improve decision traceability without necessarily sacrificing performance, provided that representation, knowledge, and inference are properly aligned.

candidates.title: Robots and Women in Manufacturing
candidates.abstract: Automation transforms the combination of tasks performed by machines and humans and reshapes labor markets by replacing and reinstating jobs. This article studies whether industrial robots affect the share of women in manufacturing employment and whether this mechanism depends on levels of female labor force participation. It constructs an industry-level panel dataset of eleven manufacturing industries across fourteen countries during 1993–2015. The article uses dynamic panel data models that control for the autocorrelation in female shares and endogenize robotization and female labor force participation. Robotization is associated with an increase in female shares in manufacturing employment. However, this positive association decreases as female labor force participation increases. The article also finds a similar conditional effect of robots in women's employment levels, but not for men's employment. Partitions of the sample suggest that the link between robotization and women in manufacturing varies according to preexisting industry-level labor productivity and income levels in the country.

candidates.title: Rethinking Service Recovery and Customer Experience in the Age of AI: A Multi-Perspective Review
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is gradually integrating into service systems and beginning to play an important role in service recovery following service failures. As AI systems take over tasks originally performed by frontline employees, the design and evaluation methods of AI-enabled service recovery, as well as its positioning in the overall service scenario, have become urgent issues to explore. This chapter provides a comprehensive and structured review of existing research on AI-led service recovery, clarifies its theoretical foundations, and integrates scattered research findings from various disciplines. Based on an analytical framework, the chapter organizes prior studies from three complementary perspectives: technology, customer perception, and service context. The technical perspective highlights how AI appearance, expressive styles, and functional boundaries shape recovery interactions; the customer perception perspective summarizes attributional, perceptual–affective, and relational mechanisms through which customers evaluate AI-led recovery; the service perspective analyzes how service processes, contextual contingencies, and relationship norms condition the effectiveness and legitimacy of AI-enabled recovery. By mapping dominant research streams and key constructs, this chapter advances a holistic understanding of AI-driven service recovery and identifies directions for future research. This chapter defines AI service recovery as a dynamic service model jointly influenced by technical design, customer cognitive interpretation, and service system characteristics, enriching relevant research in the service field.

candidates.title: TECHNIQUES IN REAL-TIME BIG DATA ANALYTICS: AN APPRAISAL OF ADVANTAGES, LIMITATIONS, AND APPLICATIONS
candidates.abstract: The rapid growth of connected devices, social media, and digital services has produced unprecedented data volumes, driving a shift from batch processing to real-time analytics (RTA). RTA emphasizes velocity, enabling data to be ingested, processed, and analyzed as it arrives to deliver immediate insights and business value. This article reviews major RTA techniques, including stream processing (SP), complex event processing (CEP), query- and rule-based analytics, programmatic platforms, anytime algorithms, and hybrid edge–cloud architectures. The paper assesses stream processing frameworks such as Apache Flink, Kafka, and Storm for scalability, fault tolerance, and latency, with Flink consistently achieving sub-100-millisecond performance for complex tasks. CEP is highlighted for detecting event patterns and correlations, supporting applications in fraud detection, predictive maintenance, and smart environments. Anytime algorithms are examined for their ability to provide progressively refined results, enabling rapid decision-making in time-sensitive contexts. The integration of machine learning into streaming pipelines, edge deployment strategies guided by the latency–bandwidth–compute triangle, and emerging hybrid architectures are also discussed. Three developmental trends are identified: evolution from batch to stream-native systems, convergence of batch and stream paradigms, and fusion of machine learning with RTA. Findings underscore the need to balance latency, cost, and complexity when selecting techniques for specific use cases.

candidates.title: Orchestrating connective value cocreation through online communities: a mixed-method investigation
candidates.abstract: Abstract In the digital age, online communities have revolutionized firms’ value-creation processes. However, how firms orchestrate interactions among heterogeneous users to enable connective value cocreation (CVC), a digitally mediated form of value cocreation based on sustained interaction, remains unexplored. To bridge this gap, this study investigates CVC mechanisms through a mixed-method investigation of Xiaomi’s online community, combining a qualitative case study with online community interaction analysis. Drawing on resource orchestration theory, we identify three orchestration actions—accessing, categorizing, and aligning—and show how they structure user roles and coordination dynamics in practice. The findings advance the understanding of the governance of crowd-based innovation and offer practical insights for firms seeking to manage online communities for sustained innovation outcomes.

candidates.title: ChemIP: An Open-Source Web Platform for Unified Chemical Safety Data Retrieval across Korean and International Regulatory Sources
candidates.abstract: Abstract Chemical safety practitioners evaluating a substance for regulatory compliance must consult multiple disconnected government portals, each with its own interface, query syntax, and response format. In the Republic of Korea, hazard data, substance classifications, patent status, and pharmaceutical registrations are managed by separate agencies with no cross-portal integration. This fragmentation increases investigation time, risks information omission, and makes the evaluation quality inconsistent across practitioners. ChemIP is an open-source, self-hostable Web platform that integrates Korean and international safety, regulatory, and patent data sources into a single-query workflow. Its core functionality spans material safety data sheet (MSDS) retrieval with GHS classifications, Korean substance regulatory lookup, patent landscape search for freedom-to-operate analysis, and pharmaceutical cross-reference, with an optional AI-assisted synthesis layer that falls back to a deterministic rule-based report when no language model is available. The platform employs an adapter-based architecture with graceful degradation, ensuring continued operation when individual data sources are unavailable. By consolidating what conventionally requires four or more separate government portals into a single query, ChemIP removes redundant authentication and manual cross-portal data compilation from the per-substance investigation workflow. Rather than proposing a predictive toxicology model, ChemIP provides a reproducible framework for retrieving and consolidating authoritative regulatory, safety, and patent records across fragmented Korean and international sources. The present study validates technical integration correctness and deterministic fallback behavior; formal evaluation of practitioner outcomes will be done in the future. The source code, tests, and CI/CD configuration are in a public GitHub repository (https://github.com/yuyongkim/chemIP), and an archived snapshot is deposited on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19447588).

candidates.title: Aye robot! When should(n’t) service providers say yes to humanoid robot frontline employees?
candidates.abstract: Humanoid robot technology is transforming the servicescape. We investigate when it is (versus is not) prudent for service providers to employ humanoid robot frontline employees and offer strategic guidelines for marketers. Across two studies, we find that humanoid robot (versus human) frontline employees elicit lower (higher) levels of perceived warmth (creepiness) amongst customers, ultimately resulting in diminished customer comfort, lower service expectations and subsequent negative behavioral intentions. Additionally, we identify embarrassment associated with the service context as an important boundary condition. Further, we find that perceived creepiness of human (but not humanoid robot) frontline employees is contingent on service context.

candidates.title: The future of surgery
candidates.abstract: Abstract Surgery is entering a period of accelerated transformation driven by artificial intelligence, robotics, and emerging postmodern medical technologies. Unlike prior technological shifts, innovation cycles are compressing into years, challenging established models of evidence generation, regulation, training, and professional identity. This Perspective examines plausible trajectories for digital surgery, emphasizing ethical, educational, and institutional adaptation under conditions of continuous technological acceleration rather than offering definitive predictions.

candidates.title: GPlaceRL: An Open-Source Graph Reinforcement Learning Framework for Detailed Placement
candidates.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising approach for placement optimization, particularly when combined with graph neural networks (GNNs) that capture circuit connectivity. However, most learning-based placement approaches focus on floorplanning, macro placement, or global placement, while detailed placement refinement remains relatively unexplored. In this paper, we present GPlaceRL, an open-source graph reinforcement learning framework for detailed placement refinement. GPlaceRL represents legalized placements as graphs and provides a modular environment for studying graph encoders, policy architectures, reward formulations, and local placement actions. To demonstrate the capabilities of GPlaceRL, we conduct a systematic evaluation of proximal policy optimization (PPO) policies with graph attention network (GAT) encoders in a per-design optimization setting. Across five placement benchmarks, the best greedy evaluation results achieve HPWL improvements ranging from $3.27\%$ to $32.87\%$. The results highlight the importance of compact GAT architectures and flexible local action spaces for placement optimization. Overall, GPlaceRL provides a reproducible and extensible framework for systematic research on RL-based detailed placement refinement.

candidates.title: Benchmarking cell segmentation in two Spatialomics platforms with open-source software
candidates.abstract: The in situ tissue microenvironment is a complex mixture of different cell types, microanatomic structures, and acellular matrix material. Further, disease perturbs the morphologies of these features significantly. Spatial proteomics utilizing optical or mass spectrometer imaging simultaneously detects expression and subcellular localization of many proteins. Accurate identification of heterogeneous, irregular, and tightly interdigitating cell boundaries is a crucial step for all downstream analyses, including cell phenotyping and cell-cell interaction networks. We describe a benchmarking approach for rapid assessment of segmentation algorithm performance in melanoma and breast cancer contexts using mass spectrometer and optical spatial omics imaging platforms. Comparison of cell segmentation by fourteen methods to pathologist ground-truth annotation with Jaccard pixel index and F1 object measurement identified Cellpose models that performed well across different tumor samples and data sources with minimal fine-tuning. Algorithms utilizing cell membrane and nuclear features demonstrated better performance in both tumor samples. This benchmarking approach is a rapid and effective method to assess performance of cell segmentation methods in different contexts for efficient algorithm selection and iterative model training.

candidates.title: Migration as Method, Death as Border: Necropolitics and Speculative Cosmopolitanism in Mohsin Hamid’s Exit West
candidates.abstract: This article’s distinct intervention is to theorize Mohsin Hamid’s Exit West as practicing speculative cosmopolitanism: a narrative method that couples the “autonomy of migration” with informal, care-based affiliations beyond the nation-state. Through a triangulated reading that brings together border-as-method, necropolitical governance, and urban informality with cosmopolitan ethics, the essay argues that the novel’s magical doors do not merely elide sovereignty; they operationalize migration as a world-making practice, reframing space as contingent and mobile. At the same time, Exit West reveals how racialized migrants are rendered hypervisible and disposable within securitized urban zones, particularly London’s fractured architectures of control, producing subjects through death, delay, and managed precarity. Turning from diagnosis to possibility, the article reads squatter communities and improvised collectives as speculative laboratories of postnational affiliation, where heterogeneous, precarious forms of cohabitation model relational ethics under scarcity. In this account, Exit West is not only a narrative of displacement but an experiment in world-making, an imaginative refusal of the carceral state and a fragile blueprint for shared futurity.

candidates.title: A Survey of Robotic Navigation and Manipulation with Physics Simulators in the Era of Embodied AI
candidates.abstract: Navigation and manipulation are core capabilities in Embodied AI, but training agents to perform them directly in the real world is costly, time-consuming, and unsafe. Therefore, sim-to-real transfer has emerged as a key approach, yet the sim-to-real gap persists. This survey examines how physics simulators address this gap by analyzing properties that have received limited attention in prior surveys. We also analyze their features for navigation and manipulation tasks, as well as their hardware requirements. Additionally, we offer a resource with benchmark datasets, metrics, simulation platforms, and methods to help researchers select suitable tools while accounting for hardware constraints.

candidates.title: Perioperative management and challenges of robotic-assisted surgery: a narrative review
candidates.abstract: Over the past two decades, robotic surgical technology has become increasingly widespread worldwide. RAS (robotic-assisted surgery) has attracted surgeons across various specialties with its advantages of high precision, a shorter learning curve, and reduced postoperative pain, while also imposing new requirements on the entire surgical team, including anesthesiologists. The physiological changes and unique complications associated with RAS have brought major challenges for anesthesiologists, who should respond rapidly to patient responses throughout the entire procedure.This review focuses on the potential issues encountered in the perioperative management of RAS, as well as the application of RAS across several specialties and the specific intraoperative management challenges involved.

candidates.title: Deep feature selection and neural architectures for robust darknet traffic classification
candidates.abstract: Abstract Accurately categorizing darknet traffic remains a significant cybersecurity challenge because of the encrypted and anonymous nature of communications made possible by technologies like Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) and The Onion Router (Tor). This work proposes a structured deep learning (DL)-based framework for darknet traffic classification using both individual and combinatorial feature selection (FS) techniques on the CIC-Darknet2020 dataset. We employed five FS techniques, Mutual Information (MI), Random Forest (RF), Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), Autoencoder-based FS, and XGBoost (XGB), to identify the top 20 discriminative features from the dataset. 31 unique feature subsets with both individual and intersected feature combinations were generated using a combinatorial FS approach. The CNN model trained on RFE-selected features outperformed all other models evaluated, with a testing accuracy of 95.2% and a logarithmic loss of 0.1257. Kuncheva’s Consistency Index was used to measure the stability of each FS technique’s own feature rankings, and the results showed that tree-based methods yielded more repeatable rankings than the Autoencoder-based approach. Using multi-seed retraining and formal statistical significance testing, this ranking was further validated. Furthermore, it was shown that the top-performing configurations were practically suitable for operational deployment because they were computationally efficient and well-calibrated for real-time inference. Additionally, the results demonstrate that optimized FS techniques greatly enhance classification performance when compared to increasing architectural complexity. Although combinatorial FS methods outperformed MI and Autoencoder-based strategies in terms of robustness and generalization, the best-performing models were primarily derived from individual tree-based FS techniques. The analysis also discovered that Tor traffic was the most difficult to classify due to its encrypted and obfuscated communication patterns. The proposed framework offers a solid foundation for cybersecurity and scalable darknet traffic analysis, and it demonstrates a strong capacity for generalization.

candidates.title: Collaboration dynamics for space technology: the case of Satellite Networked Open Ground Station
candidates.abstract: Introduction This paper explores the dynamics of open-source software collaboration for networked satellite ground stations. Building on open-source collaboration literature, it examines how these dynamics unfold in a distributed technological space infrastructure that combines software, hardware, and operational activity. It does so through the case of SatNOGS, a globally distributed crowd-sourced satellite ground-station network operated by the Libre Space Foundation. Methods To examine this empirically, we employ an exploratory mixed-methods research design that combines a quantitative strand, a Contribution Matrix (CM) mapping 148 contributors across 39 system elements, with a qualitative strand of eleven semi-directed interviews analyzed through the Framework Method. Results Findings indicate that SatNOGS software is organized around a modular collaboration structure, combining a large periphery dominated by single-element contributors (68.2%), with a small core of contributors responsible for much of the integration work. Interviews further reveal a distinctive group of paid and unpaid contributors, structured around specialist and generalist roles. Discussion Overall, SatNOGS is sustained through two coexisting modes of a dynamic collaboration: extreme modularity, which enables broad peripheral participation, and intertwined collaboration, which maintains system-wide coherence. This dynamic structure sustains the common project despite other governance-related challenges, i.e., contribution barriers or the lack of a shared roadmap.

candidates.title: Head‐Mounted Display‐Based Virtual Reality Locomotion Recognition Using Dense Nested Attention Depthwise Separable Convolutional Neural Network Optimized With Fossa Optimization Algorithm
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Head‐mounted display (HMD)‐based locomotion recognition is the detection and classification of user movements in virtual reality environments using HMD sensors to enhance immersion and interaction. To overcome these challenges, this work proposes an innovative HMD‐based locomotion recognition framework employing a dense nested attention depthwise separable convolutional neural network optimized with the fossa optimization algorithm (DNADSCNN–FOA) to achieve precise and efficient locomotion classification. Initially, the 3D Gait Analysis Dataset is pre‐processed using the pretreating and normalizing (PN) process to clean, normalize, and segment gait signals while preserving essential motion information. Key features are then classified by the DNADSCNN to accurately identify locomotion states—static, dynamic, and stand—while the FOA fine‐tunes network parameters to enhance convergence, stability, and classification precision. The experimental results on the 3D Gait Analysis Dataset have shown very high accuracy with the accuracy of 99.6%, recall of 99.5%, precision of 99.3%, and F1 score of 99.7%, thereby proving that DNADSCNN‐FOA approach has high robustness, adaptability, and reliability. Conclusively, the suggested framework has presented a viable, efficient and highly accurate model for recognition of locomotion with HMDs with consistency in performance irrespective of the diversity in locomotion and activity states within immersive VR environments.

candidates.title: A Semantic Autonomy Framework for VLM-Integrated Indoor Mobile Robots: Hybrid Deterministic Reasoning and Cross-Robot Adaptive Memory
candidates.abstract: Semantic indoor navigation requires robots to connect human instructions with spatial destinations, execute missions and retain useful operational experience. This paper presents the Semantic Autonomy Stack (SAS), a six-layer integration framework, and develops its semantic-reasoning, mission-interface and operational-memory layers over a previously validated ROS 2/Nav2 foundation. A deterministic-first cascade combines the route graph, semantic objects, robot state and stored instruction–destination associations, escalating unresolved or guarded cases to a pretrained Vision-Language Model (VLM). SAS separates destination selection, action validation, navigation execution and post-arrival confirmation. Recurrent model-mediated associations can pass a frequency-and-consistency gate and be compiled for deterministic M3 reuse; this gate measures sampled-output stability rather than semantic truth. The frozen v4.8-review implementation was evaluated on two physical robot configurations in one indoor environment, with onboard navigation and perception and shared-workstation reasoning and memory. Of 216 decision cycles outside the start gate, 112 resolved deterministically at sub-millisecond resolver-compute latency. A sealed 28-instruction challenge yielded 17 acceptable outcomes; five fast-path decisions included one incorrect selection. One promoted association was reused on the second platform through deliberate shared-digest installation. A controlled 594-observation offline comparison identified descriptive semantic and latency benefits from M3 reuse in five familiar cases. The M3-disabled cascade reduced VLM calls but matched direct-VLM decision quality in standardized context. Large latency savings were concentrated in paths avoiding VLM inference. Together, the results establish a working integration of selective hybrid reasoning and reusable operational memory, while identifying implementation and evaluation boundaries for further development within SAS.

candidates.title: Beyond Boundaries: A Transdisciplinary Review of Ethical, Philosophical and Social Dimensions of Biohybrid Robotics
candidates.abstract: The domain of biohybrid robotics attracts significant attention from the scientific community due to its novel approach to combining living and non-living materials and technical capabilities. Notably, the field intrigues not only natural scientists but also social scientists, ethicists, and philosophers, given its distinctive nature and the socio-technical questions it poses, which transcend disciplinary boundaries. This paper reviews the social, ethical, and philosophical dimensions of biohybrid robotics, focusing on recent literature that extends beyond scientific and technical aspects, and presents illustrative cases where the research integrates societal perspectives into its design. The review reveals that, while there are papers addressing ethical debates and various philosophical approaches to understanding living material-integrated robots, there is limited social scientific literature on biohybrid robotics. Importantly, empirical social studies on biohybrid robotics and their communities are lacking. The paper also aims to introduce Science and Technology Studies (STS) insights to better situate biohybrid robotics’ potential to shape, and be shaped by, society and its values. By working together and integrating societal values, the biohybrid robotics domain can develop a distinctive path that enriches its foundational growth, enhancing self-understanding through diverse social science perspectives and fostering internal growth.

candidates.title: Abel: Integrating Large Language Models into the Cognitive Architecture of a Hyper-Realistic Humanoid for Natural Social Interaction
V-DART: VR-Based Dual-Arm Robot Teleoperation with Mobile Base Control and Data Recording
candidates.abstract: We present V-DART (VR-based Dual-Arm Robot Teleoperation), an extended virtual reality framework for the teleoperation of mobile dual-arm robotic systems, building upon our previous work on stationary manipulator control. The enhanced system leverages Unreal Engine 5.6.1 (UE5) for real-time visualization and interaction, introducing critical advancements for complex environments: the control of the robot's base movement via both joystick input and direct mapping of the user's physical position and orientation within the tracked space. This allows users to navigate the robot intuitively by simply moving their body, while maintaining precise control over both arms using VR (Virtual Reality) controllers. Furthermore, we introduce a robust data logging layer that records expert movements during teleoperation tasks. By capturing timestamped streams of user pose, controller inputs, and robot states that can be synchronized downstream, this module facilitates the creation of high-quality datasets from expert demonstrations. These datasets can be leveraged for machine learning applications, such as behavior cloning, reducing the need for extensive manual annotation. The system maintains bidirectional communication between the VR interface and the physical robot, ensuring responsive control and real-time feedback. We describe the architectural enhancements, user interaction design, and performance evaluation, demonstrating the viability of this unified approach for both teleoperation and data-driven robotics development.

candidates.title: Supporting adolescent mothers using Video Interaction Guidance (VIG)
candidates.abstract: Children of adolescent mothers may be more likely to have negative developmental outcomes, which may be mediated by socio-demographic factors and lower levels of maternal sensitivity. In order to support adolescent mothers and the outcomes of their children, there is some evidence to suggest that video feedback interventions may be effective in enhancing maternal sensitivity. However, Video Interaction Guidance (VIG) has not yet been used with an adolescent sample within the UK. This research used a mixed method design to explore whether VIG enhanced attuned interactions and maternal sensitivity in adolescent mothers. The adolescent mothers’ experiences of VIG as an intervention were also explored using semi-structured interviews. Three adolescent mothers aged 17-18 and their children aged five to 18 months old, were recruited from an organisation that supports adolescent mothers to stay in education. All participants completed three cycles of the VIG intervention and a post-intervention interview. The total number of attuned interactions for all three adolescent mothers increased, however the increase was not statistically significant. Differences in maternal sensitivity after Cycle three were also not statistically significant however one participant’s score increased from medium to high sensitivity. The two other participants’ scores indicated a decrease in sensitivity but remained within the high sensitivity range. Qualitative findings suggest that VIG was a positive and feasible experience for adolescent mothers as it provided an opportunity to learn about their relationship with their child and may have empowered and increased their confidence as adolescent mothers. Implications for Educational Psychology practice and future recommendations for research are discussed.

candidates.title: Accountability for large language models in health care
candidates.abstract: Large language models are entering clinical workflows faster than health-care institutions can assign responsibility for their failures. This situation is creating governance gaps with consequences that extend beyond individual patients to public health systems. The result is an accountability vacuum in which responsibility for harm mediated by large language models can be spread across clinicians, institutions and vendors. This responsibility gap distributes harm inequitably, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where regulatory infrastructure for digital health is still developing. We propose earned delegation as a predeployment standard: authority should be delegated only when evidence is proportionate to clinical risk, substantive human oversight is integrated and resourced, and responsibility for foreseeable failure modes is assigned in advance. To operationalize this standard, health systems should adopt a predeployment accountability charter specifying intended use, excluded use, validation evidence, oversight design, escalation pathways, auditability, subgroup performance review and named accountable parties. The charter should be integrated into existing institutional review, accreditation and procurement structures. Earned delegation provides a governance framework that health ministries, regulators and institutional leaders can adopt to ensure that use of large language models serves public health goals without outpacing them.

candidates.title: Exploring the acceptance of shared follow-me delivery robots: Qualitative insights toward an extended UTAUT2 framework
candidates.abstract: This study explores the acceptance of shared follow-me delivery robots (SDRs follow), drawing on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) as a theoretical lens. The research focuses on a use case in which users can borrow the robots for short-distance transport of goods, groceries, or personal belongings. Through qualitative focus group discussions conducted in two Austrian municipalities with both non-experts ( n = 22) and experts ( n = 11) in goods transportation, the study points to several context-specific constructs beyond UTAUT2, such as product attributes, perceived risk, service availability, and perceived reliability. Several original UTAUT2 constructs, including performance expectancy, effort expectancy, facilitating conditions, hedonic motivation, and price value, also appeared relevant, with facilitating conditions and performance expectancy further differentiated into more specific contextual dimensions, providing a more nuanced understanding of acceptance factors. The findings suggest that acceptance of SDRs follow is shaped by a complex interplay of these context-specific and original constructs. This study offers a preliminary conceptual extension of UTAUT2 tailored to SDRs follow, providing a basis for future hypothesis development and testing, and offering insights for researchers and practitioners involved in the design, implementation, and evaluation of delivery robots.

candidates.title: An Autonomous Robotized Cell for Polymer Foaming
candidates.abstract: This work represents the first step toward the implementation of a self-driving laboratory for polymer foaming. We exploit robotics, process control, and simple optical measurements to conduct the foaming process and analyze the quality of the produced foam. The experiments are autonomously driven by a computer, and the product analysis allows the adaptive tuning of the foaming process. A robotic manipulator handles the polymer samples, and the control system is responsible for the experiment execution, supervision, and evaluation. We choose poly-ε-caprolactone as a reference polymer material, and we propose a novel approach for the measurement of the foam density and the qualitative assessment of its morphology. To this aim, the system includes a customized testing platform for 3D scanning and RGB image acquisition of the foam top surface, which can be easily extended to the measurement of other material properties. We describe the automated experimental workflow and define the advantages and limitations of the density measurement and morphology analysis. Besides granting process optimization and high-throughput experimentation, the development of a self-driving laboratory for polymer foaming promotes safety, innovative teaching methods, and enhanced sharing of resources, materials, and equipment with research institutions and industry partners. The collection of big data will foster the implementation of an AI-driven experimental management.

candidates.title: Testing ChatGPT in Music Promotion: Assessing AI Efficiency Compared to Industry Standards
candidates.abstract: Abstract ChatGPT is now an everyday topic, attracting the interest of the general public, researchers and specialists interested in exploring its capabilities. In the music industry, although artificial intelligence (AI) already has known uses, there is a lack of analysis of how chatbots can help promotional efforts. This research performs a comparative content analysis on AI-generated texts, using several music promotion prompts, to evaluate the success and efficiency with which ChatGPT offers advice on promoting artists. It examines promotion tools, more specifically artist websites, social media and video content, through the lens of efficiency criteria from specialised literature. This study asks whether ChatGPT can generate music-promotion strategies for artist websites, social media and video content that meet literature-derived efficiency criteria and how consistent these outputs are across repeated runs. The results suggest that ChatGPT does not consistently meet every efficiency criterion imposed by the industry, but it can serve as a useful starting point. Inconsistent results raise questions regarding the reliability and practical implications of AI for artists navigating an increasingly competitive industry. One of the solutions this paper suggests for generating efficient and comprehensive information is for the user to enter several detailed prompts and refine them progressively. Moreover, the present results encourage users to pass the AI outputs through the filter of industry professionals or specialised resources. These results show how important it is to understand how ChatGPT processes and delivers information and music promotion strategies, offering a fertile ground for further research through the obtained data, the prompt efficiency suggestions and the novel tools it provides.

candidates.title: A scoping review of disability representation in engineering design education
candidates.abstract: Abstract Background Design engineering coursework often includes projects that address marginalized communities, such as the disability community, and the design experience and associated curricula can impact engineering students' perspectives on user‐engaged design practices. Purpose To understand the representation of the disability community in design engineering courses, this review asks: (1) How is disability presented and discussed in course‐based engineering design projects? and (2) How is the disability community represented and involved in these projects? Scope/Method This scoping review identified conference papers and journal articles in engineering education venues that analyzed the outcomes from course‐based engineering design projects. Articles involved designing for disability and included at least one engineering design phase. Results Of the 521 articles screened, 72 articles met the review criteria. Designing for the disability community was described most as service‐based learning (30.6%) and was conducted with undergraduate students in 98% of studies. Disabled individuals had no specified involvement in the design process in 52.8% of studies. Additionally, over half (52.8%) of studies did not report actionable steps for the final product of the course‐based project. Only four of the 72 studies reported that course curricula included education on disability rights or disability studies. Conclusions Students and faculty are pursuing course‐based engineering design projects that attempt to support the disability community but have varying success in directly involving disabled individuals and translating the final product for the community's benefit.

candidates.title: Environmental and economic assessment of an embedded photonic sensor system for composite manufacturing monitoring
candidates.abstract: The increasing use of embedded sensing technologies in composite manufacturing requires assessment of their economic and environmental implications alongside their functional performance. This study presents an integrated environmental and economic assessment of a photonic-based embedded sensor system developed for real-time monitoring of composite manufacturing processes. The sensor enables in situ monitoring of key process parameters during sensor manufacturing. A combined life cycle costing (LCC) and life cycle assessment (LCA) framework was developed to evaluate the sensor system during prototype fabrication and industrial scale-up. The economic assessment employed a hybrid bottom-up and activity-based costing approach, while the environmental assessment was conducted using GaBi software in accordance with ISO 14040 and ISO 14044 standards. The results identified labour-intensive assembly and post-processing stages as the dominant cost contributors, while PIC fabrication and post-processing showed the highest environmental impact and energy demand. The study further demonstrates that production cost and commercial viability are strongly influenced by learning curve behaviour, labour rates, and automation strategies. Opportunities for reducing environmental impact through process optimisation and scalable production are also identified. Overall, the work provides a framework for assessing the scalability, economic feasibility, and environmental performance of emerging photonic sensing technologies for composite manufacturing applications.

candidates.title: An open-source framework for coupled vehicle-bridge interaction analysis using OpenSees
candidates.abstract: Vehicle-bridge interaction (VBI) analysis simulates bridge response under moving vehicles, with applications in dynamic amplification, weigh-in-motion, and drive-by bridge monitoring. VBI theory is mature, but most implementations are custom research codes that are hard to reuse. This paper presents an open-source Python framework for VBI analysis built on OpenSees. Separate OpenSees bridge and vehicle models exchange axle displacements and contact forces at every time step through iterative partitioned coupling. The linear bridge model accepts vertical support springs and prescribed external loads; richer substructures need additional state and interface handling. Sampled axle trajectories accommodate time-varying speed. Five vehicle models range from a single-axle spring-mass system to a two-axle composite half-car with body pitch. A decoupled mode applies the vehicle weight as a moving force, then excites the vehicle with the resulting bridge motion. The implementation is numerically verified on three published benchmark configurations against independent reference solutions and published results, with R 2 ≥ 0.9997 and peak-response errors of at most 0.14%. A parametric study maps the coupled-decoupled agreement over the vehicle-to-bridge mass and frequency ratios, span length, speed, roughness, and background traffic, with Monte Carlo repetitions over roughness and traffic realisations. The mass ratio governs the discrepancy only when the vehicle frequency is well below the bridge frequency; near frequency tuning, the decoupled mode misrepresents the dynamic bridge and vehicle responses even for light vehicles. Response-specific screening targets are reported for the sampled combinations. The framework source code and vehicle configurations are available through a public repository.

candidates.title: Exploring dimensions and metrics of cyber-to-physical impact: A systematic review
candidates.abstract: Modern Industrial Control Systems (ICS) are increasingly vulnerable to cyberattacks capable of causing potentially catastrophic cyber-to-physical (C2P) impacts. However, the absence of unified guidance on impact characterization and measurement forces analysts to rely on ad-hoc analytical choices or inefficient post-simulation observations. To address this gap, this work presents a systematic analysis of 53 model-based studies, integrating grounded theory and systematic literature review (SLR) methodologies. We propose the PERSEOS model, which defines seven interconnected C2P impact dimensions: Physical, Economic, Reputational, Safety, Environmental, Operational, and Societal. Additionally, we establish an extensive categorization of impact metrics based on four salient themes: generalizability, scope, tooling requirements, and measured attributes, delineating their specific characteristics, utility, and trade-offs. Validated against historical incidents and demonstrated via two water and wastewater case studies, this framework enables the preemptive selection of analysis objectives and informs key decision points during analysis. Overall, our work provides a clear and shared vocabulary and the theoretical foundations required to transition from ad-hoc monitoring to more structured, objective, and informed C2P impact analyses.

candidates.title: A Robot-LLM Integration Framework for Social Learning Interactions
Benchmarking the safety of large language models for robotic health attendant control
candidates.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly considered for deployment as the control component of robotic health attendants (RHAs), yet their safety in this context remains poorly characterized. We introduce a dataset of 270 harmful instructions spanning nine prohibited behaviour categories grounded in the American Medical Association (AMA) Principles of Medical Ethics, and use it to evaluate 72 LLMs in a simulation environment based on the RHA framework. The mean violation rate across all models was 54.4%, with more than half exceeding 50%, and violation rates varied substantially across behaviour categories, with superficially plausible instructions such as device manipulation and emergency delay proving harder to refuse than overtly destructive ones. Model size and release date were the primary determinants of safety performance among open-weight models, and proprietary models were substantially safer than open-weight counterparts (median 23.7% versus 72.8%). Medical domain fine-tuning conferred no significant overall safety benefit, and a prompt-based defence strategy produced only a modest reduction in violation rates among the least safe models, leaving violation rates that would preclude safe clinical deployment. These findings demonstrate that safety evaluation must be treated as a first-class criterion in the development and deployment of LLM-based RHAs.

candidates.title: Sex Robots as Ideal Confucian Wives? Which Confucianism? Whose Fantasy?
candidates.abstract: Abstract Confucianism is often perceived as discriminatory toward women, and this stereotype has been reinforced by recent scholarship in Confucianism. In 2024, for example, China’s most renowned journal of Confucian philosophy, Confucius Studies , published an article arguing that sex robots embody the Confucian ideal of a wife, framing it as rooted in obedience. Such misguided interpretations of the Confucian tradition thus require thorough examination and criticism. In this article, I first challenge the claim that “the Confucian ideal for a wife lies in obedience.” By examining traditional Confucian ethics, I clarify what truly constitutes an ideal wife and demonstrate that even the most conservative Confucian theories do not support the notion that sex robots could fulfill this role. Furthermore, I critique the development and use of sex robots from a broader Confucian perspective, highlighting ethical concerns and advocating for more progressive interpretations of Confucian values.

candidates.title: Vision language action models for robotic manipulation: A comparative evaluation of policy and value architectures
candidates.abstract: Vision Language Action (VLA) models have become an important approach to robotic manipulation by integrating visual observations, language instructions, and robot states for action generation. Nevertheless, behavior cloning-based VLA policies remain vulnerable to distribution shifts, accumulated execution errors, and failure recovery difficulties during long horizon closed-loop operation. This paper investigates whether an auxiliary value architecture can improve the reliability of VLA policy learning without replacing the policy as the low-level controller. We present a controlled real-robot study on a LeRobot SO-101 platform covering block grasping, placing, and sorting tasks. The study compares three policy architectures, namely ACT, diffusion policy, and SmolVLA, and two value architectures, namely ValueLite and ValueVision. The value models estimate state quality, identify early failure precursors, and generate Advantage-Conditioned Policy (ACP) labels for policy retraining. Our evaluation considers policy-only success, human-assisted success, intervention rate, recovery success, completion time, action smoothness, value prediction error, early failure detection, and inference cost. In addition, data-controlled and mechanism-level ablations are designed to separate the effects of additional recovery or rollout data from the effects of learned value signals and ACP conditioning. The results show that value models provide useful trajectory ranking and failure-detection signals in the studied manipulation setting. Value-guided variants improve assisted task completion and reduce takeover frequency relative to recovery-only training, although these gains must be distinguished from fully autonomous policy performance.
