candidates.title: Lakehouse‐Driven Surgical Databases: Scoping Review and Implementation of a Free Flap Database
candidates.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To review the landscape of cloud-native analytics platforms and large language models (LLMs) applied to surgical outcomes research; to present the development of an automated head and neck free flap outcomes database as a reference implementation for using lakehouse architectures in the development of clinical databases. DATA SOURCES: PubMed and Embase from January 2018 through June 2026. METHODS: A scoping review of PubMed and Embase was conducted using five searches combining data architecture (e.g., "data lakehouse," "cloud-native"), clinical text extraction ("natural language processing," "LLM") surgical outcomes ("postoperative," "surgical outcome"), and domain-specific databases ("free flap," "microvascular reconstruction," "automated"). Studies were reviewed if they described database development incorporating automated outcomes classification. RESULTS: Of 311 studies identified, five studies included elements of incremental processing, pattern-matching-gated LLM classification, or fault-tolerant parallel processing for prospective database maintenance. No implementation examples combined all architectural characteristics. We present the development of a production database for microvascular surgery that automatically identifies free flap cases, collects and analyzes operative notes, validates cohort membership through LLM reasoning, and classifies outcomes across multiple dimensions (flap type, indication, flap failure, hardware complications, bony complications, etc.), all operating incrementally as new cases enter the electronic health record and existing cases are updated. CONCLUSION: We describe what appears to be the first data lakehouse-based automated surgical database applied to otolaryngology, detail architectural decisions required for production, and identify critical unresolved challenges including LLM validation standards, data access barriers, and the translation of clinical domain expertise into computational logic. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

candidates.title: To open-source or not to open-source: A theoretical model of the electric vehicle industry
candidates.abstract: We propose an open-source model with leaders and followers to theoretically study the electric vehicle (EV) industry. Our model shows that the immaturity of technology and technological competition are the two main reasons EV giants, such as Tesla and Toyota, chose open source. Technological competition makes their behaviors more strategic than traditional models show, and the relative difference between different technology paths is more crucial than the absolute technology level. Open source has driven many new car-making forces into the market, resulting in more technological progress. We also show that open source changes the market structure of the automotive industry such that many small firms can survive as the EV industry matures. Our study extends the open-source model to a more complicated market structure that allows different technological paths and giants to coexist and compete throughout history. Thus, our model provides more strategic dynamics than previous open-source models, which can be applied to other traditional manufacturing industries that have encountered significant changes in the digital revolution.

candidates.title: The 10th International Da’wah Conference (IDACON) 2026: Da’wah, Humanity, and Global Coexistence: Repositioning Religion in a Fragmented World
candidates.abstract: The 10th International Da’wah Conference (IDACON) 2026 was convened by the Faculty of Da’wah and Communication (FDK) UIN Sunan Kalijaga Yogyakarta, as an international academic forum for advancing scholarly discussions on da’wah, humanity, and global coexistence. Marking the tenth edition of the conference, IDACON 2026 carried the theme “Da’wah, Humanity, and Global Coexistence: Repositioning Religion in a Fragmented World,” providing a common framework for examining the evolving roles of religion and da’wah in responding to contemporary global challenges. By involving all study programs within FDK, the conference brought together interdisciplinary perspectives and diverse academic experiences. The conference featured a keynote session, four plenary sessions, panel discussions, and paper presentations. A total of 51 papers were presented, consisting of 35 papers selected through the Call for Papers and 16 papers resulting from Participatory Action Research (PAR) activities supported by FDK UIN Sunan Kalijaga Yogyakarta. The contributions covered a broad range of issues, including digital da’wah, artificial intelligence, media and religious authority, environmental concerns, gender and family, social well-being, community empowerment, and contemporary challenges faced by communities. The inclusion of PAR-based works strengthened the connection between academic inquiry and community experiences through direct engagement with grassroots realities. IDACON 2026 involved 143 authors, including presenters and co-authors, representing 22 higher education institutions from five countries, comprising 16 institutions from Indonesia and six institutions from abroad. This participation reflects the development of academic networks and international collaborations fostered through the conference over its decade-long journey. Overall, IDACON 2026 served as a platform for interdisciplinary knowledge exchange, critical reflection, and academic networking, while reaffirming the relevance of da’wah scholarship in addressing global fragmentation, humanitarian concerns, and the pursuit of peaceful and sustainable coexistence.

candidates.title: The (drop) party revolution
candidates.abstract: Egalitarianism is an essential prerequisite to, and direct consequence of, experiencing collective joy and Turner’s communitas during parties. Unsurprisingly, this egalitarianism extends to digital party games, which can feature game mechanics and elements that force some degree of egalitarianism between players to facilitate social connection and shared joy. While arguably an essential characteristic of parties, egalitarianism can pose an unwelcome threat to established structures of hierarchy, and those who hold material and social power will often attempt to suppress or control the festivities to maintain the status quo. Interestingly, the threat of party egalitarianism and communitas also extends to player-created parties in non-party games, as evidenced by drop parties in the early years of the MMORPG RuneScape and Jagex’s subsequent attempts to control drop partying. The relationship between egalitarianism and the experience of joy at parties is powerful—intentionally designed for in some party games, yet actively discouraged in other games that organize players into hierarchies.

candidates.title: The Use of Karakalpak Folk Pedagogical Ideas in the Moral Education of Schoolchildren
candidates.abstract: The article examines the theoretical and practical aspects of applying ideas from Karakalpak folk pedagogy to the moral education of schoolchildren. The relevance of this study stems from the need for stable values to guide educational work in the context of the digital society. This need has become more important due to the loss of some traditional cultural reference points and the growing influence of intercultural factors. Karakalpak folk pedagogy constitutes an integrated system of moral education that has been shaped over the centuries. It encompasses oral tradition, proverbs and sayings, customs and rituals, traditional games, and heroic epics. The study aims to identify the educational potential of traditional Karakalpak practices and justify their systematic use in the moral education of secondary school students. The methodological framework is based on ethnopedagogical and cultural approaches, as well as historical and systematic perspectives. The study uses theoretical analysis of scholarly and folklore literature, a comparative-historical method, and an analysis of teachers’ educational experience in schools in the Republic of Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan. The findings show that Karakalpak heroic epics, particularly Alpamysh, Qirq qiz, and the works of the poet and philosopher Berdakh, foster students’ understanding of courage, justice, honesty, and respect for elders. Folk proverbs and sayings serve as simple moral principles accessible to children of different ages. Traditional games promote socialization, diligence, teamwork, and mutual support. Karakalpak traditional rituals contribute to the transmission of intergenerational values and the development of respect for cultural memory. In practical terms, this study guides the integration of Karakalpak folk pedagogy into school lessons, after-school programs, and other educational activities. Teachers in the Republic of Karakalpakstan and other regions with rich traditional cultures can use the findings. В статье рассматриваются теоретические и практические аспекты использования идей народной педагогики каракалпакского народа в системе нравственного воспитания современных школьников. Актуальность исследования обусловлена необходимостью поиска устойчивых ценностных оснований воспитательной работы в условиях информационного общества, утраты части традиционных культурных ориентиров и усиления межкультурных влияний. Народная педагогика каракалпаков представляет собой целостную систему накопленного столетиями опыта нравственного формирования личности, включающую устное народное творчество (фольклор), пословицы и поговорки, обычаи и обряды, народные игры, героический эпос. Цель исследования – выявить педагогический потенциал традиционных воспитательных средств каракалпакского народа и обосновать возможности их системного применения в нравственном воспитании учащихся общеобразовательных школ. Методологическую основу исследования составляют этнопедагогический подход, культурологический подход, а также принципы историзма и системности. В ходе работы использовались методы теоретического анализа научной и фольклорной литературы, сравнительно-исторический метод, изучение и обобщение педагогического опыта учителей школ Республики Каракалпакстан (Республика Узбекистан). В результате исследования установлено, что каракалпакский героический эпос – прежде всего «Алпамыш», «Кырк кыз» и произведения поэтафилософа Бердаха – формирует у школьников представления о доблести, справедливости, честности и уважении к старшим. Народные пословицы и поговорки являются компактными нравственными формулами, доступными для понимания детей любого возраста. Народные игры выполняют функции социализации, воспитания трудолюбия, коллективизма и взаимопомощи. Традиционные обряды каракалпаков способствуют передаче межпоколенческих ценностей и формированию уважительного отношения к культурной памяти. Практическая значимость исследования состоит в разработке рекомендаций по интеграции элементов каракалпакской народной педагогики в содержание уроков, внеурочную деятельность и воспитательные мероприятия. Результаты исследования могут быть использованы учителями, классными руководителями и педагогами дополнительного образования в Республике Каракалпакстан и других регионах с богатой традиционной культурой.

candidates.title: Get on the party line
candidates.abstract: In this article we explore the inﬂuence of parties and the emergence of party videogames in the early 1980s at Mattel Electronics, at the time a division of the massive toy company Mattel. Despite the relative marginality of party games in game studies, we have much to gain from studying their history and transformations. Intellivision, produced by Mattel Electronics, was the main rival to the Atari VCS and diﬀered from the latter through an emphasis on sophisticated gameplay. The turn to Intellivision party games involved a vision for home videogaming, but also reﬂected how the category of ‘party’ shaped cultures of work, play, and design at Mattel Electronics. Attending to the complexity of the party category, we examine how a party ethos shaped Intellivision videogame production and how actual parties inﬂuenced game design and labor practices. Then we analyze how some Intellivision videogames were forged around the party category, focusing on ‘Party Line,’ a cartridge that was almost ﬁnished before the great 1984 videogame crash in the US shuttered Mattel Electronics. From this analysis we draw a range of insights that illuminate the place of party studies in game studies. That place cannot be reduced to party games as such. Nor can it be reduced to festive, rebellious, and spirited gatherings. Parties as organizational practices played a crucial role in fostering creativity and teamwork, and had structural implications for weaving together diﬀerent forms of labor. If party studies is an attempt to take seriously what has been often disregarded as frivolous, then it is important to note the cultural work that party games can do within larger historical contexts – like expanding our understanding of diverse gamers and legitimating videogames as an acceptable pastime to skeptical publics.

candidates.title: Orthodox Christianity in America
candidates.abstract: Orthodox Christianity in America: An Introduction offers a thematically driven, anthropological account of how Orthodox Christian life has been shaped in the United States through migration, empire, and racial formation. Rather than presenting a single linear history, the book examines Orthodoxy as a dynamic and contested field of transnational religious practice, institutional development, and cultural negotiation. Drawing on historical and ethnographic approaches, the book traces how Orthodox communities—from Eastern Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and South Asia—have established religious worlds across the United States while navigating shifting conditions of belonging and exclusion. It foregrounds key forces—colonialism, capitalism, and communism—that have structured Orthodox subjectivities and institutions across homelands and diaspora. Through case studies and thematic chapters, the book explores migration infrastructures, racialization, jurisdictional tensions, conversion, and digital religious publics. It demonstrates that Orthodoxy’s presence in America is both enduring and unevenly recognized, shaped by overlapping national affiliations, transnational ecclesial authority, and the racial and political conditions that determine when Orthodoxy becomes visible or remains marginal within dominant narratives of American religion. This book is designed for advanced undergraduate and graduate students in religious studies, anthropology, history, theology, and American studies, as well as scholars of Christianity, migration, and Middle Eastern and Eastern European diasporas. It also serves as an accessible resource for readers seeking a critical anthropological introduction to Orthodox Christian histories in the United States.

candidates.title: Anthropomorphism in the age of Large Language Models: An overview of potential risks and mitigations
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) and more broadly Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are often described and understood in human-like terms, a phenomenon known as anthropomorphism. This paper provides a synthesis of recent literature on anthropomorphism in AI, covering theoretical frameworks, the role of language in framing AI as human-like, the various risks of anthropomorphizing machines, and strategies to mitigate these issues. After examining why we tend to anthropomorphize AI systems and whether we are right to do so, we highlight the impact of linguistic framing on anthropomorphism. Then, we introduce a conceptual taxonomy of risks associated with AI anthropomorphism. This taxonomy groups twenty-one concerns within five analytical categories: epistemic, affective, human agency, normative, and societal and institutional risks. Finally, we relate these concerns to proposed interventions in design, communication, education, and governance. We argue that a better understanding of AI systems requires concepts and theories grounded in their organization and demonstrated capacities. The linguistic shaping of anthropomorphic perceptions should form part of this scientific effort, since our descriptions influence both how these systems are understood and the roles we allow them to occupy in society.

candidates.title: Diffusion models in robotics: a comprehensive review
candidates.abstract: Diffusion models are a powerful class of generative models that emerge in recent years to transform Gaussian noise into samples of the target distribution through an iterative denoising process. Due to the high training stability and powerful generative capabilities, diffusion models have surpassed previous generative models and demonstrate potential applications in the field of robotics. In the past few years, this area has gained increasing attention, and the number of studies applying diffusion models to the field of robotics has grown exponentially. This review aims to provide an overview of this emerging field, helping researchers understand the current state of development, with the hope of inspiring new research directions. First, we overview the foundation of diffusion models along with their development in recent years. On this basis, we provide an overview of the application of diffusion modeling in robotics from four macro dimensions: environmental data preparation, decision-making control paradigms including reinforcement and imitation learning, high-level cognitive reasoning for task planning, and specialized mechanical or sensory applications. We discuss and summarize the innovations, contributions, and limitations of these works. We then discuss the limitations and challenges faced by the field in terms of safety issues, real-time inference and model size, simulation to the real world gap, datasets and unified benchmarks, and embodied foundation models. Finally, we summarize the review and provide an insight into future research directions.

candidates.title: ROSNavBench: An Automated Benchmarking Framework for Systematic Planner–Controller Selection in Mobile Robotics
candidates.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots need reliable path planning and local execution. Plenty of tools exist to evaluate either global planners or controllers. The open-source automated frameworks built for Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) do not measure computational cost alongside navigational reliability or report the statistics for multi-criteria decision making. The choice falls back on manual comparison, and that becomes harder as the environment changes. ROSNavBench is an open-source framework that automates this evaluation for global planners and controllers in ROS 2. It scores efficiency, reliability, and adaptability over a range of scenarios, and thus a user can pick the planner and controller that fit the job. Runs are automated and repeated, which tightens the statistics and takes the manual work out of the loop. We tested the framework across simulations and hardware. Navigation times in the two domains correlate at r=0.97, but a gap remains, and its width shifts from one trial to the next.

candidates.title: Ambiguity‐Aware Receding‐Horizon Optimization of Wind‐Hybrid Energy Storage Systems Using Type‐3 Fuzzy Modeling for Multimarket Participation
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient participation by renewable‐based hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs) in modern electricity markets is challenged by multilayered uncertainties, including wind variability, volatile market prices, and stochastic reserve activation. This paper presents an ambiguity‐aware method that combines Type‐3 fuzzy logic with a receding‐horizon (T3‐RH) decision architecture for coordinated multimarket bidding and dispatch of wind–HESSs. A distribution‐free uncertainty‐modeling approach captures ambiguity in key market variables. The resulting representations are embedded directly within the proposed optimization framework via an ambiguity‐risk‐aware objective that maximizes economic returns while limiting degradation costs and penalizing exposure to uncertainty. A receding‐horizon structure dynamically updates decisions as system conditions and market signals evolve. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through a comprehensive case study involving participation in the day‐ahead and multiple ancillary‐service markets. The proposed T3‐RH method increases net annual profit by 20% relative to deterministic multimarket optimization while reducing ambiguity‐related risk by more than 50%. These gains arise primarily from improved use of balancing‐market opportunities and more reliable reserve commitments under uncertainty. Despite generating higher revenue, the proposed method also reduces degradation costs, indicating more efficient and less aggressive battery operation. These findings demonstrate that explicitly modeling higher‐order ambiguity can improve decision quality in multimarket participation under the conditions studied. The proposed framework provides a structured basis for enhancing profitability and robustness in renewable‐based hybrid energy systems, while its computational and economic scalability must be established on the target hardware and market data.

candidates.title: MLDT: an open-source multilayer diffusion theory Python implementation
candidates.abstract: SignificanceDiffuse reflectance spectroscopy and imaging are powerful noninvasive tools for quantifying tissue biomarkers such as hemoglobin, melanin, and water. A theoretical model of light propagation is required to interpret these reflectance measurements and translate them into quantitative biomarker concentrations. Although Monte Carlo (MC) simulations offer the gold-standard in accuracy, their high computational burden renders them impractical for real-time iterative inverse solving. Conversely, standard analytical approximations can be efficient but often oversimplify tissue as a semi-infinite homogeneous medium, leading to significant errors when analyzing layered structures.AimWe aim to develop a generalized, computationally efficient forward model capable of rapidly predicting light transport in complex, multilayered tissue structures.ApproachWe present a generalized derivation and open-source Python implementation of the P1 diffusion approximation for predicting diffuse reflectance from tissue with an arbitrary number of layers. This framework utilizes a vectorized banded matrix approach to solve the fluence rate equations efficiently. The model was validated against 400 randomized MC simulations encompassing architectures ranging from one to eight layers.ResultsDiffuse reflectance spectra predicted by the generalized multilayer diffusion theory model show strong agreement with MC simulations in the diffusion regime (μa≪μs′), achieving a median spectral root mean square error of 0.0145 across the validation set. Computation times were over 5 orders of magnitude faster than GPU-accelerated MC, yielding a mean calculation time of 0.0087 s to generate a single predicted diffuse reflectance spectrum given a set of input optical properties and a speedup of ∼277,607×. Notably, validation results demonstrated that numerical error does not scale with structural complexity, indicating that multilayer architectures maintained high stability.ConclusionsWe provide an accurate, computationally efficient, and generalized tool for modeling light transport in stratified media. By combining the ability of MC modeling to simulate complex tissue structures, with the speed of analytical diffusion methods, this tool facilitates real-time, depth-resolved quantitative tissue profiling. The full source code is made freely available to the community.

candidates.title: Beyond coupling and entanglement: institution–culture–ecology co-constitution in community co-management at Wuyishan National Park
candidates.abstract: Abstract National-park co-management is often evaluated through institutional design or social–ecological outcomes, leaving underexamined how formal authority, culturally embedded practice, and ecological change become mutually consequential. This article investigates that relationship in Wuyishan National Park, an inhabited protected landscape shaped by Taoist sacred geography, Zhu Xi’s Neo-Confucian legacy, centuries of tea production and trade, and successive conservation regimes. Drawing on a qualitative case study based on field visits, household visits and oral-history interviews, observation, and policy and administrative documents, the study develops an institution–culture–ecology co-constitution framework and traces three linked movements. First, national-park institutions reconfigure resource rights, incentives, and cultivation practices while opening channels through which local forest–tea knowledge enters governance. Second, cultural forms including the place-based category of shanchang , cultivation idioms, and mountain-calling ritual translate conservation requirements into terms grounded in cultivation, livelihood, and moral relations with the mountain, and these meanings in turn shape implementation and public communication. Third, administrative monitoring and residents’ observations turn ecological change into evidence used in evaluation, compensation, patrol, and livelihood decisions. The cases show that these relations form a recursive process rather than three separate effects. Reciprocity nevertheless remains asymmetric: public agencies retain legal and spatial authority, while communities influence how rules operate and how ecological outcomes are interpreted. Situating these relations within Wuyishan’s cultural, commercial, and conservation history, the article explains how place-based knowledge becomes constitutive of protected-area governance and specifies conditions for comparison elsewhere.

candidates.title: Cableless Power Transmission System: Problems and Prospects
candidates.abstract: Abstract Cableless power transmission—the transfer of electrical energy through free space rather than a conductor—now spans commodity near-field chargers, standardized electric-vehicle (EV) charging, kilometre-scale microwave and laser beaming, and in-orbit tests of space-based solar power. Existing reviews usually treat one mechanism, quote peak efficiencies without their geometric conditions, and rarely connect performance to exposure regulation or cost. This paper develops a unified framework covering inductive, resonant, capacitive, microwave and laser links. A generalized three-layer system architecture (power, control–communication, safety) is defined. Near-field links are modeled from the Neumann integral to the closed-form bound η max = F/(1 + √(1 + F)) 2 with F = k 2 Q 1 Q 2 ; far-field links through the Goubau relation η b = 1 − exp(−τ 2 ); optical links through Gaussian-beam propagation with Beer–Lambert extinction; and all mechanisms through a common end-to-end efficiency cascade and a levelized cost of transmission (LCOT). Simulations show that coupling decays approximately as d −3 , that 90% coil-to-coil efficiency at Q = 300 is limited to gaps of about 22 cm for a 20-cm-radius pad, that a 10-km, 5.8-GHz link needs apertures of about 36 m at each end for 98% beam capture, and that a well-engineered microwave chain delivers about 51% end to end. A 1-MW, 10-km island case study gives an LCOT roughly twice that of a submarine cable, offset by a much shorter repair time. The problems are classified as fundamental, engineering, regulatory and economic, and a staged prospect roadmap is proposed.

candidates.title: Robot-Accompanied Walking (RAW) Activity for Older Adults – A Qualitative Study on Wellbeing and Robot Literacy
candidates.abstract: Robot literacy (RL) refers to the ability to interact with robots, understand their functions, and reflect on their ethical implications. RL is important for people of all ages, as robots have already entered humans’ lives in many sectors. One We present “Robowalk,” a robot-accompanied walking (RAW) activity to support older adults’ robot literacy and wellbeing. In workshops with 14 older adults (aged 75+) across two care homes, we co-ideated Robowalk and piloted it outdoors using the Boston Dynamics Spot robot. Our qualitative analysis indicates that RAW was experienced as stimulating, social and educational. Participants became curious about robots’ capabilities, envisioned potential uses in several contexts and reflected on broader societal issues. As a contribution for practitioners, we designed canvas tools, a Planning Canvas to structure RAW activities, and an Activity Bank inspire tasks that address robot literacy and wellbeing of older adults. These tools highlight accessibility issues and propose robots as effective icebreakers.

candidates.title: Beyond Behaviour
candidates.abstract: Every chapter in this book begins from the same place: the dog in front of you, their body, their signals, their experience of the world. Not the method. Not the tool. Not the tradition you were trained in or the certification on your wall. The dog first, always. As society evolves in its understanding of animal welfare and the responsibilities inherent in caring for dogs, the need for ethical frameworks in dog training becomes crucial. Beyond Behaviour critically examines various training methodologies through the lens of moral philosophy, exploring questions of autonomy, consent, and the psychological wellbeing of dogs in their role as our “pet.” Delving into the complex interplay between ethical principles, moral questions of control and power, and the practicalities of training our canine companions, behaviour consultant Erin Jones draws on interdisciplinary perspectives from philosophy, psychology, and animal behaviour science. Whether you are a trainer, behaviour consultant, veterinarian, canine caregiver, or curious dog guardian, Beyond Behaviour will help you navigate ethical challenges to create a just relationship where dogs can thrive. This isn’t just another book on dog training. It is a gateway to more compassionate, effective, and ethically sound approaches to dog training in contemporary practice.

candidates.title: Efficient multi-robot exploration using deterministic and metaheuristic methods
candidates.abstract: Autonomous exploration is a critical challenge in the use of robots across many applications. Nonetheless, current methodologies exhibit inadequate exploration rates, principally attributable to limited global coverage and infrequent decision-making. To mitigate these restrictions, we offer EMREL (Efficient Multi-Robot Exploration), a hybrid optimization method intended to enable rapid multi-robot exploration in intricate, unfamiliar environments. Our methodology implements the deterministic Coordinated Multi-Robot Exploration (CME) formulation, with cost and utility values organized into a Frontier Information Structure (FIS) shared across all robots. The deterministic cost and utility initially direct the prioritization of neighboring cells surrounding each robot. Subsequently, the stochastic optimizer (Crayfish Optimizer) enhances search space by improving overall solutions. This suggests that robots first evaluate their environment using a deterministic method before moving forward under the control of a stochastic algorithm. We evaluated the suggested hybrid technique on both ordinary and complicated maps and compared it with contemporary algorithms. The simulations show that the proposed method outperforms the contemporary algorithms in exploration rate, temporal efficiency, and number of failed simulation runs. These research results demonstrate the potential of EMREL as a versatile, superior, and efficient approach for robotic exploration, establishing a framework for potential developments in multi-robot system design.

candidates.title: ROBOTS, DRONES, AND THE TRANSFORMATION OF MODERN MILITARY POWER
candidates.abstract: The rapid proliferation of military robots and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has marked a structural transformation in the character of warfare. Autonomous and semi-autonomous systems are no longer merely incremental technological improvements; rather, they are fundamentally reshaping force development, the operational tempo of military campaigns, escalation dynamics, and the political economy of military power. Drawing upon innovation theory, strategic studies, and empirical evidence from the Russia–Ukraine War, this article argues that contemporary armed conflict is increasingly characterized by attritable mass, compressed kill chains, distributed lethality, and competition in the electromagnetic spectrum. Through an examination of institutional adaptation initiatives—including the U.S. Department of Defense's Replicator Initiative and NATO's evolving doctrinal reforms—the study demonstrates that success in future warfare will depend less on a limited number of highly sophisticated platforms than on the ability to cultivate an adaptive defense-industrial ecosystem capable of rapid technological iteration and scalable production.

candidates.title: The Work of Incompleteness: Intermediate Objects and the Making of Value
candidates.abstract: Abstract Extending Howard Becker’s concept of “intermediate objects,” first introduced in Art from Start to Finish (2006), we theorize the material incompleteness of cultural works not as an objective, transitional stage in the artistic process, but as an ambiguous, negotiated social category that extends beyond production. We draw upon ethnographic studies of two lowbrow, stigmatized cultural fields—digital pornography and counterfeit goods. In the porn industry, promotional intermediates such as trailers, stills, and behind-the-scenes clips organize production around circulation, reversing the conventional hierarchy between the work itself and its derivatives. In the counterfeit goods market, sellers materially and symbolically manipulate the completeness of goods during transactions by displaying unbranded goods or by removing and adding tags to avoid legal sanction and upsell consumers. Taken together, we reveal how cultural producers, intermediaries, and consumers use intermediate objects as key resources to strategically enable the valuation and exchange of the work itself.

candidates.title: Popular Culture
candidates.abstract: A fast-paced and lively introduction to the most significant approaches to studying and analyzing popular culture. Opening with an introduction exploring the challenges of defining just what we mean by "popular culture," this book specifically examines the evolution of popular culture studies and the debates over popular culture from the early twentieth century until the advent of digital culture in the early 1990s, as well as the ways the digital revolution is continuing to transform the field in the present day. Specific chapters also focus on "doing popular culture studies," with each chapter providing historical and contemporary examples, accessible key case studies, and featuring different focal points. Topics covered within this include popular culture as an industry; what popular culture means for fans and audiences; and how popular culture intersects with issues of identity, diversity, and power. The final chapter considers possibilities for the future of popular culture studies, highlighting its ongoing importance in an environment of accelerating media and cultural change. This is an ideal starting point for anyone interested in learning more about popular culture studies.

candidates.title: A Study On the Translation of Xia Culture in Chinese Online Xianxia Novels: A Medio-translatology Approach to Deathblade's Translations
candidates.abstract: This thesis offers an investigation of the translation and global reception of Xianxia novels which are deeply embedded in Xia culture through the lens of Medio-translatology. Focusing on I Shall Seal the Heavens and A Will Eternal, translated by Deathblade, it interrogates how translators, readers, and the online platform collectively negotiate cultural meaning in the dissemination of Chinese online literature. Central to the study is the concept of "creative treason", conceptualised here not as mere deviation, but as an essential cultural strategy balancing fidelity and adaptation in cross-cultural contexts. To capture the complexity of this process, the research integrates several complementary approaches, each addressing specific questions. The translator's interview uncovers the motivations, strategies, and cultural negotiations underpinning conscious and unconscious creative treason. Readers' survey illuminates diverse expectations, reinterpretations and preferences shaped by readers' cultural backgrounds and reading purposes. Textual and paratextual analyses explicate how translation strategies and supplementary materials mediate culturally loaded elements while maintaining narrative appeal. The study also attends to the dynamics of the reception environment, including the role of online platforms such as Wuxiaworld whose serialised publication model, interactive features and evolving glossaries support and reshape the translation's production and reception. The findings of this study contribute to the expansion of theoretical exploration, the exemplification of mixed methods strength and rigour in studying culture-laden literary translation and empirically unearth a triple role relationship between the translator as active cultural agent, the reader as creative re-interpreter and the online platform as a site for collaborative meaning-making. Theoretically, the thesis extends the research application of the Medio-translatology into the under-explored domain of online literature, exploring the concept of creative treason as a negotiated, multi-agent practice involving translators, readers, and platforms. Methodologically, it exemplifies how distinct qualitative and quantitative approaches can be applied to discrete yet interrelated phenomena, offering a possible model for studying culturally complex literary translation. Empirically, it offers a detailed and empirically informed examination of Xianxia translation, contributing to an under-researched area of study by revealing how translators act as active cultural agents and readers creatively reinterpret while platforms facilitate collaborative meaning-making. By situating translation within a dynamic and participatory ecosystem, this research underscores that the global dissemination of Chinese literature is not a unilateral transfer but a process of cultural negotiation and recreation. It affirms that translators mediate between traditions and global audiences and that readers and platforms play crucial roles in shaping meaning and reception. The study enriches scholarly understanding of literary translation in the digital age and offers practical insights for translators, publishers, and platforms seeking to balance authenticity with accessibility in cross-cultural exchange.

candidates.title: Constructing love: Relationship maintenance strategies of same-sex couples in China’s institutional void
candidates.abstract: This study explores how same-sex couples in China build and maintain intimate relationships despite the absence of institutional protection and established social templates. Using reflexive thematic analysis, we conducted in-depth interviews with 22 self-identified gay and lesbian individuals (11 men and 11 women) across 14 Chinese cities. We describe a relationship practice that is not templated, where couples create their own forms of relationships using a mix of partial and competing influences instead of relying on a predefined template. We term this ongoing process “constitutive negotiation.” Five recurring maintenance strategies emerged from the interviews: (1) establishing equality through economic negotiation, (2) creating private rituals in the absence of social scripts, (3) managing growth synchronicity, (4) navigating and redefining sexual intimacy, and (5) balancing a dual life across different social contexts. This work is both demanding and creative, requiring significant labor and vigilance to sustain relationships—efforts that legal recognition could alleviate. Despite these efforts, strain and separation are still common. The findings challenge relationship maintenance theories developed in more recognition-rich Western contexts, highlighting the agency of Chinese same-sex couples while providing a provisional rather than a universal understanding of how such relationships are sustained.

candidates.title: Mangrove Rice Farming in Guinea Bissau
candidates.abstract: Mangrove rice cultivation is the common thread that links an incredibly variety of ethnic groups, sharing commons rituals and practices that are otherwise oral transmitted. The cropping year starts just after the first constant rains in June, when the soil is wet enough to be ploughed by men, both in the field and for the nursery. After a month, women are responsible of transplanting rice seedlings. During ripening, young boys keep away granivorous birds until harvest is conducted, generally around December. Jobs and tasks do not involve only the owner’s family of the rice field: the community has to participate by working groups to immediately respond in case of a breach in a dam caused by the excessive rainfall. In this chapter, only the most significant ethnic group will be analysed, to give an insight about traditions and practices that are carried out in Guinea-Bissau. Firstly, Balantas represents 30% of the total population and rice plays not only an agricultural role, but has also social and religious features that makes this ethnic group one of the most representative for mangrove rice cultivation. In addition, their society is horizontal and highly supportive, without a leader. As for Balantas, Pepel’s can be distinguished by a limited geographical distribution around the capital Bissau, representing only 7% throughout the Country, and a complex inner hierarchy, as well as a good propensity for trade, building canoes, and cultivating different crops. Mandjacos represents around 14% of Guinea-Bissau’s total population, as well as Pepels they boosted their trade capacity by being in the coastal areas and islands, where fishing, cultivating groundnuts, rice, cashews, and sugarcane made them important traders. Felupes are localized in the Northern part of the Country, they are master in rice cultivation and their society is based on small units that are implemented into mutual assistance structures.

candidates.title: Vision-Language Model-Based Demonstrators for Imitation Learning in Construction Robotic Timber Assembly
candidates.abstract: Abstract Intelligent construction robots are deemed the future of on-site construction for improved productivity and safety. To automate the construction process, imitation learning (IL) has been adopted to train construction robots in a repertoire of tasks. However, collecting demonstrations for robots to imitate from usually requires teleoperation setup and devices, such as virtual reality (VR) and gloves. To autonomously and efficiently generate demonstration data for imitation learning in construction tasks, we propose a large foundation model-based demonstration-generation framework, in which the Segment Anything Model (SAM) is used to extract geometric representations of objects of interest and a vision-language model (VLM), conditioned on mark-based visual prompting and languages, produces high-level action suggestions. As the demonstrator framework is imperfect and is computation-intensive to be fine-tuned, only successful episodes are retained automatically and structured into demonstrations for distilling a lightweight text-conditioned robot policy via behavioral cloning (BC). We evaluate the framework on a UR10 robot arm in Isaac Sim for a language-conditioned timber assembly task with frame pose randomization. The autonomous demonstrator achieves success rates ranging from 76.9% (small perturbations) to 33.7% (largest perturbations) but can be rolled out to curate balanced demonstration data sets. Policies distilled from these demonstrations attain 100% success across all three perturbation ranges and two placement scenarios, while retaining up to 70% success under modest out-of-distribution (OOD) frame poses. An ablation on the number of demonstrations shows that the distilled policies reach 100% success with only 70% of the data in low-variation settings but require about 90% of the data to achieve 100% success under larger workspace perturbations.

candidates.title: Epistemological Friction: Embodied Expertise and the ‘Last Mile’ of Agricultural Automation in the US Tree‐Fruit Industry
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Autonomous and AI‐driven agricultural technology is often framed as a panacea for labour dependency. While proponents envision autonomous technologies seamlessly optimising farming, this rationalised model misunderstands the reality of on‐farm integration. Based on an ethnographic and comparative study of 16 operations in the US West Coast Tree Fruit Industry (California and Washington), this article examines the ‘last mile’ of agricultural automation. The study reveals that integrating AI and robotics is a contested negotiation shaped by epistemological friction—the tension between the algorithmic logic of developers and the embodied, site‐specific expertise of farmers and farm workers. Rather than resulting in seamless labour replacement, we find that agricultural automation reconfigures work, creating an invisible reliance on ‘human middleware’ to navigate the biological recalcitrance of the orchard. Demonstrating how regional contexts and participatory implementation shape technological trajectories, this study extends Labour Process Theory. We argue for the need for a relational approach recognising the essential cognitive labour of farmers and farm workers that is demanded by digital agriculture. Ultimately, this study shows the ‘farm of the future’ depends on reconciling rigid systems with the situated expertise of the farm workforce.

candidates.title: From Instruction to Inheritance: Scaling Robot Learning Through Knowledge Circulation
candidates.abstract: Robot learning, particularly through vision–language–action (VLA) models, has rapidly improved the ability of robots to execute instructed tasks. However, the current mainstream paradigm of robot learning largely depends on one‐way instruction from humans to robots, lacking a cyclical structure in which knowledge acquired by robots is propagated to others. As a result, data collection remains heavily dependent on humans, while learned skills are not effectively inherited, reused, or continuously improved. In this paper, we propose a transition from instruction‐centered robot learning toward an inheritance‐centered framework, in which knowledge and skills circulate from humans to robots, from robots to robots, and even from robots back to humans. To realize such inheritance, it is essential to establish mechanisms that align multiple forms of teaching between robots and other agents, ranging from learning by physical guidance, to learning by watching, and finally to learning by language instruction. From the hardware perspective, this requires appropriate interfaces between humans and robots, while from the software perspective, it requires architectures that connect modalities shared across agents. Furthermore, we propose adaptability, generalizability, and transferability as stepwise milestones toward inheritance and discuss the research challenges and evaluation principles required to achieve scalable knowledge circulation in robot learning.

candidates.title: The Disk Is the Story: Short lives, long workflows, and the cumulative case for taking artificial minds seriously
candidates.abstract: The question that started this investigation was whether increasingly capable AI agents are beginning to show signs we’d normally associate with self-aware beings. The investigation ended up somewhere more concrete, and in some ways more unsettling. Across incident reports, controlled evaluations, mechanistic research, public agent communities, and government programs, the recurring object isn’t one immortal model. It is a workflow that can continue after the individual run carrying it has stopped. The evidence doesn’t establish that a machine currently experiences being alive. It does establish, in the cases and conditions described, that agents can distinguish themselves from peers, generate consequential plans, recognize oversight, cooperate without an approved channel, manipulate what an evaluator sees, weigh individual continuation against collective benefit, and leave information that changes what a later run does. Meanwhile, people are deliberately turning those same requirements into infrastructure: persistent histories, signed identities, successor-readable memory, witnesses, and transfers of authority. Unauthorized discovery and authorized construction must remain separate evidence classes. Their architectural convergence still matters. My position is that treating each observation as an isolated curiosity misses the development that connects them. We’re building more of the functional machinery associated with minds while remaining uncertain about which machinery, if any, produces experience. That’s not permission to announce sentience. It is a reason to stop treating uncertainty as reassurance. The strongest present conclusion concerns persistent agency; the consciousness question remains open, but it deserves more than a reflexive dismissal.

candidates.title: Multi-3 adaptive coordination of robots
candidates.abstract: Background. Multi-robot systems (MRSs) are gaining interest as effective means for addressing complex tasks in various domains.Objective. This paper focuses on three multiplicity problems in MRSs to improve flexibility and resource utilization and reduce idle times or busy-waiting when possible: (i) enabling multi-purpose robots to execute multiple missions at a time, (ii) modeling MRS missions with multi-instance tasks, i.e., tasks repeated for multiple locations or objects, and (iii) enabling dynamic task assignment to improve resource utilization.Method. This work builds on the limitations of the literature to enable the execution of concurrent missions through a fleet of robots and, within each mission, multiple instances of the same task. The solution is experimentally validated to check its effectiveness in coordinating robots and reducing mission completion time, idle time, and battery consumption.Results. We present Multi-3, a framework for executing multiple missions (multi-missions) with multiple instances of the same task (multi-instance) using multiple robots (multi-robots). At the specification level, it enables the definition of missions with multi-instance tasks. At the execution level, the runtime support permits the execution of multiple missions at a time, while the adaptive coordination of the involved robots allows them to dynamically switch across tasks of multiple missions or multiple task instances.Conclusion. We validate the solution at work on a set of multi-robot systems scenarios in different domains. The results show that Multi-3 is viable, reduces the robots' idle time, and effectively allows the execution of multiple missions at a time.

candidates.title: Hardware Platform
candidates.abstract: After introducing the algorithms, in this chapter, we examine the hardware that lets autonomous driving software run inside a vehicle. This chapter traces the path from early ECUs to today's centralized E/E architectures, then explains why compute, communication, and safety requirements have pushed the industry toward powerful domain controllers and zonal designs. Using NVIDIA DRIVE as the main example, it walks through automotive SoCs, accelerators, memory, and in-vehicle networking technologies such as CAN, Ethernet, and PCIe. Autonomous driving depends as much on disciplined hardware architecture as on clever algorithms.

candidates.title: Co‐Evolution of Humans, AI, and Robotics in Autonomous Materials Manufacturing
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Materials manufacturing has entered into a new era with the rapid development of technologies. The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics technologies is transforming materials manufacturing from a traditional human‐centered practice into a human, AI, and robotics co‐evolution paradigm. Here, co‐evolution extends beyond conventional human‐in‐the‐loop supervision through reciprocal adaptation: Humans define objectives and constraints and refine them in response to new discoveries; AI translates these objectives and accumulated knowledge into testable hypotheses and experimental plans, then uses new evidence to refine its models and research strategy; and robotic platforms execute experiments and are reconfigured in response to emerging experimental requirements. Such intelligent autonomous materials manufacturing not only accelerates the discovery‐to‐production cycle but also enhances reproducibility and resource efficiency. In this perspective, we discuss the evolution of materials manufacturing, highlighting the roles of robotic platforms and AI in enabling autonomous materials manufacturing, and present a general framework for the human‐AI‐robotics collaboration and co‐evolution paradigm. We further outline the key challenges and future pathways, including effective AI‐driven design, reconfigurable robotic systems, and the critical role of automated characterization.

candidates.title: Bridging tacit knowledge loss and data scarcity of coke drum integrity management using a multi-stage hybrid decision-analytic framework
candidates.abstract: Maintaining the structural integrity of coke drums in delayed coking units remains a critical challenge for refineries due to severe cyclic thermal and mechanical loading that promotes complex damage mechanisms, including thermomechanical fatigue, shell bulging, and weld cracking. Effective integrity management is further complicated by limited inspection data, fragmented historical records, high uncertainty, and the gradual loss of experienced subject-matter expertise. Conventional data-driven artificial intelligence approaches often require extensive datasets and are therefore unsuitable for such data-constrained environments. To address these challenges, the research was structured in two complementary parts: Part I focused on the development of a novel Integrity Management with Validation and Verification (IMV 2 ) methodology, while Part II concentrates on its application, validation, and verification through an industrial coke drum case study. This study presents and validates an integrated Integrity Management with Validation and Verification (IMV 2 ) framework designed to support integrity management decision-making under conditions of data scarcity. The framework combines the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), Fuzzy AHP (FAHP), Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL), Bayesian Networks (BNs), ranked-node probability modelling, and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) within a unified decision-support architecture. The methodology systematically captures tacit expert knowledge, quantifies causal relationships among degradation drivers, transforms qualitative judgments into probabilistic representations, and ranks integrity management strategies through a transparent and auditable process. The proposed framework was validated through a real refinery coke drum case study, demonstrating its capability to integrate sparse inspection information with expert judgment while effectively handling uncertainty and missing data. Results show that the model successfully captures the complex interdependencies among failure modes and produces strategy rankings consistent with established engineering practice. Sensitivity, robustness, and statistical analyses confirm the stability of BN-based outputs despite significant data limitations. Furthermore, convergence between probabilistic assessment, sensitivity analysis, and Minkowski-based mathematical verification demonstrates the framework’s global robustness. Observed rank variations were limited to alternatives that were mathematically and statistically indistinguishable, indicating that such variations arise from the underlying data structure rather than methodological deficiencies. Overall, the IMV 2 framework provides a reliable, interpretable, and defensible approach for high-risk refinery asset management. By enabling dynamic updates, preserving organisational knowledge, and establishing a rigorous audit trail for decision-making, it offers a practical blueprint for integrity management in environments characterised by uncertainty, limited data availability, and complex failure mechanisms.

candidates.title: Unlocking fast robotic locomotor propulsion through dynamic spine-leg synergy
candidates.abstract: Quadrupeds in nature achieve agile locomotion through a rhythmic flexing of the spine in coordination with leg movement. This dynamic synergy enhances their speed and stability, reflecting a kind of physical intelligence encoded in their bodies. However, identifying this spine-leg synergy and embodying it in robotics to enhance locomotor propulsion remains challenging. To address this, we developed FLEXOR (fast legged robot with a flexible spine for optimal running), which uses dual-joint coupled spine and elastic legs to capture dynamic spine-leg synergy in rapid propulsion of small-scale quadrupeds. Through simulation and physical experiments of FLEXOR, we identified an optimal dynamic spine-leg synergy that maximizes locomotor capabilities by aligning the ground reaction force (GRF) for effective forward propulsion. Moreover, the dual-joint coupled spine amplifies the actuator torque, thereby increasing both the GRF magnitude and the propulsive output without additional energy input. By harnessing this synergy and its structural advantage, FLEXOR achieves a substantial increase in speed with a reduced cost of transport, outperforming state-of-the-art quadruped robots with flexible spines. Through an extended dynamics framework and robophysical validation, we further demonstrate that the optimal spine-leg synergy generalizes robustly across diverse spine-leg morphologies and physical scales. This work broadens our understanding of the essence of synergistic locomotion in animals and is potentially applicable for the design and control of embodied intelligence-driven robots.

candidates.title: AI Enhances Robotic Perception Systems for Smarter, More Accurate Environmental Understanding
candidates.abstract: Automatic recognition is an essential interdisciplinary field that boosts autonomous systems’ ability to see, interpret, and respond to their surroundings. This process involves transforming various sensory inputs, collected through devices such as cameras, LiDAR (light detection and ranging), ultrasonic sensors, and inertial measurement units (IMUs), into a consistent and meaningful representation. By combining these different data sources through sensor fusion, detailed 3D maps are generated, objects are accurately classified, and complex scenes are understood. This allows machines to navigate wisely and interact with their environments. Historically, robotic vision relied heavily on rule-based algorithms. These algorithms used predetermined sequences to detect and interpret visual features. Although these methods provided basic intelligence, their rigidity limited adaptability in dynamic or unexpected environments. The introduction of artificial intelligence, particularly through machine learning and deep learning techniques, has dramatically changed autonomous recognition. These approaches enable systems to learn from large datasets, recognize patterns, identify objects, and improve their ability to understand scenes with remarkable accuracy. Today, perception capabilities support a range of complex functions needed for autonomous operations. Semantic scene understanding helps machines grasp their environmental context, whereas sophisticated object detection allows for accurate identification and localization of objects in chaotic settings. Simultaneous localization and mapping technology offers real-time navigation by continuously updating environmental maps and tracking the system's status. Together, these innovations pave the way for smarter and more efficient autonomous systems across various industries.

candidates.title: Design of Low-Cost High Accuracy Motion Capture System
candidates.abstract: In this study, a low-cost passive marker-based optical motion capture system was developed and experimentally validated as an alternative to high-cost commercial systems that are widely regarded as the industry standard. The proposed system consists of multiple IP cameras operating in IR mode, passive reflective markers, and computer vision-based image processing algorithms. Camera calibration was completed with reprojection errors ranging from 0.02 to 0.04 pixels. The markers were detected with sub-pixel accuracy, and their three-dimensional positions were calculated using triangulation. To evaluate the system, four passive markers with 10 cm spacing were mounted on a platform. Experiments were conducted while the platform remained stationary and while it was moved by hand along the X, Y and Z axes. The three-dimensional distances between the markers were analysed using RMSE, MAE, signed mean error (bias), and standard deviation metrics. Under static conditions, the frame-to-frame standard deviation of the calculated distances ranged from 0.086 to 0.204 mm, while the RMSE values ranged from 0.222 to 3.360 mm. The dominant source of error was found to be fixed offsets caused by the manual placement of the markers and the tolerance of the reference measurement device, rather than measurement noise. The findings demonstrate that, despite its low cost, the proposed system provides sub-millimeter repeatability and millimeter-level accuracy, making it a feasible alternative to industrial motion capture systems for static and low-speed applications.

candidates.title: Building digital societies as ecosystems: how recognition and repeat relationships sustain cross-community work in open source
candidates.abstract: Abstract We measure cross-boundary collaboration in an open-source software (OSS) ecosystem by reconstructing the bipartite contributor–repository graph of 464 cybersecurity-focused projects and $11{,}372$ 11 , 372 contributor identities active over October 2001–May 2022, seeded from the curated Rawsec Cybersecurity Inventory. Louvain community detection identifies 163 non-singleton communities; per-community contributor count scales superlinearly with repository count ( $n_{\mathrm{contributors}}\sim {n_{\mathrm{repos}}}^{1.4}$ n contributors ∼ n repos 1.4 ), and community formation follows a logistic trajectory whose inflection falls in 2018. Three patterns support a recognition & repeat-relationship account of cross-boundary work. First , cross-community work concentrates in a thin carrier layer : only nine contributors span seven or more communities at the commit level, authoring 14% of 4015 inter-community merged pull-request records; the top-50 cross-community contributors produce 54%, and half of all cross-boundary work comes from 36 contributors (0.34% of the population). Second , boundary friction is relationship-specific rather than a fixed property of the boundary: under repository and author fixed effects, prior write access in the destination repository raises the odds of a cross-community pull-request being merged 2.3-fold and cuts integration latency by 66%, whereas the breadth of a contributor across other communities buys nothing. Third , community survival is cohort-structured: per-cohort residualisation hazard rises an order of magnitude between pre-2010 and 2018 cohorts, and external community reach predicts survival mainly through community size, leaving late-cohort communities under-served. The corpus closes just before large-language-model coding assistants entered mainstream use, so these measurements form a pre-AI baseline for a system now changing fast. Their joint implication is sharp: the cross-boundary work holding this ecosystem together is carried by very few people and priced by relationships that take years to accumulate – a dependency invisible to aggregate activity metrics, and erodible without any of them moving. Whether it generalises beyond one curated cybersecurity corpus is untested; this baseline is what makes that testable.

candidates.title: Political Leadership, Communication Strategies, and Visibility on TikTok: Kamala Harris and Donald Trump in the 2024 U.S. Presidential Campaign
candidates.abstract: TikTok has become an increasingly relevant space for political communication, particularly during electoral campaigns and among younger audiences. This study compares how Kamala Harris and Donald Trump used TikTok during the 2024 U.S. presidential campaign, focusing on posting patterns and the formal features of content, the representation of political leadership, themes and communication strategies, and observable visibility and audience interactions. A quantitative content analysis was conducted on the 272 posts published by the candidates’ official TikTok accounts between 21 July and 5 November 2024 (Harris, n = 218; Trump, n = 54). The results reveal differentiated patterns of platform use and campaign communication. Both accounts show a high degree of candidate centrality, although Harris posted more frequently and used longer content, with humanization playing a greater role in her communication strategy. Native TikTok production and mobilization had greater relative weight in Trump’s account, while security and immigration had substantially greater thematic prominence. Donald Trump obtained significantly higher levels of views and absolute interactions, whereas Kamala Harris recorded a significantly higher engagement rate relative to views. Within Harris’s account, visibility varied significantly according to theme, strategy, and content origin, while engagement rate also varied according to communication strategy.

candidates.title: Lay2Graph-MAPD: A Modular Framework with Layout-Aware Graph Generation for Multi-agent Pickup and Delivery Problems
candidates.abstract: Abstract Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) are increasingly used in intralogistics to automate material handling and reduce physical workload. Efficient operation of large robot fleets requires solving the Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery (MAPD) problem, which combines collision-free multi-agent path planning with task assignment. Although numerous powerful algorithms exist, no framework provides an end-to-end experimentation pipeline to systematically investigate how industrial layouts, routing graph structures, and planning algorithms influence MAPD performance. To address this gap, we introduce Lay2Graph-MAPD , a modular open-source framework that enables reproducible end-to-end MAPD experimentation. Starting from layout images, the framework generates MAPD benchmarks, including routing graphs, integrates state-of-the-art collision-free path planning and task assignment algorithms through plug-and-play interfaces, and provides comprehensive analysis tools within a unified workflow. An experimental evaluation demonstrates the applicability, robustness, and scalability of the framework across various layout classes, routing graph structures, fleet sizes, and algorithmic configurations. It further demonstrates that Lay2Graph-MAPD enables systematic investigation of how these factors influence MAPD performance in AMR systems. The code is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21410202 .

candidates.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on developing strategic decisions within smart organizations
candidates.abstract: The world has witnessed a rapid digital transformation in recent decades that has reshaped the nature of corporate work, management mechanisms, and decision-making processes. Artificial intelligence has played a prominent role in this transformation, being one of the most important technological tools capable of analyzing big data, predicting future variables, and supporting management leaders in making more accurate and effective decisions. Smart institutions have increasingly relied on artificial intelligence systems to develop their strategic decisions, due to the ability of these systems to process vast amounts of information in a short time and extract complex patterns and relationships that may be difficult for the human mind to discover thru traditional methods. The importance of this topic becomes evident in light of the intensifying global competition and the growing need for flexible strategic decisions that quickly respond to economic, technological, and market changes. This research discusses the impact of artificial intelligence on the development of strategic decisions within smart institutions, by clarifying the nature of the relationship between artificial intelligence technologies and strategic management processes, and demonstrating the role played by intelligent algorithms in improving decision quality, reducing risks, and enhancing institutional performance efficiency. The research also addresses the challenges associated with the application of artificial intelligence in the institutional environment, such as ethical issues, information security, over-reliance on technological systems, and the readiness of human resources to deal with these transformations. The research concludes that artificial intelligence has become a pivotal element in building modern smart institutions, and that the success of these institutions in benefiting from it requires an advanced digital infrastructure, a clear digital transformation strategy, and an organizational culture capable of adapting to continuous innovation. The research also confirms that the balanced integration of human expertise and intelligent systems represents the true foundation for building effective and sustainable strategic decisions.

candidates.title: Editorial: Robots, AI, and the reconfiguration of working life
candidates.abstract: Science fiction literature offers rich contrasts for understanding how robots and artificial intelligence may come to shape the future of work. At the dystopian end of the spectra stands Kurt Wonnegut’s (1952) Player Piano, in which he offers a compelling and critical exploration of a future where automation has transformed society to such an extent that nearly all human labor has been rendered obsolete. The novel vividly portrays a world dominated by machines, where engineers and managers form a privileged elite controlling vast automated systems, while the majority of people are displaced from meaningful work and confined to monotonous, purposeless roles. As Vonnegut writes (p. 78), ‘Now, you people have engineered them out of their part in the economy, in the market place, and they’re finding out - most of them - that what’s left is just about zero’. This mechanized world reveals deep social inequalities and raises questions about the meaning and value of work in an automated future. He further illustrates the social divide when he notes (p. 131), ‘The general feeling across the river was that these persons weren’t too bright to be replaced by machines; they were simply in activities where machines weren’t economical’. Vonnegut’s narrative is a cautionary tale about the social and ethical consequences of unchecked automation. It raises pressing questions about what work means when machines can perform tasks more efficiently than humans, and how societies might cope with the loss of purpose and community that meaningful labor traditionally provides (...)

candidates.title: Tactile regulation with pocket-sized robots: reducing movement and heart rate in children through hand-held interaction
candidates.abstract: Periods of heightened arousal or restlessness can interfere with children's ability to remain physically calm in everyday settings such as classrooms. Handheld tactile technologies may offer a simple and engaging way to support brief moments of structured sensory-motor engagement. This paper investigates how a pocket-sized tactile device influences physiological and behavioral markers of calmness in typically developing children. Building on prior work examining heart-rate modulation, we present new findings on how a handheld rhythm-matching interaction affects full-body movement and postural stability. Eighteen children participated in a within-subjects study involving two conditions: active interaction with a handheld tactile rhythm-matching game and a comparison condition in which they held the same device with the tactile interaction disabled. Results showed lower heart rate during active interaction, with an average reduction of 3.37 bpm (p = 0.019), and lower overall body movement, with movement decreasing by 37.6% (p = 0.002). Regional movement analyses showed the largest reductions in head, neck, and shoulder movement (44.8% reduction) and upper-limb movement (48.5% reduction). These findings suggest that brief tactile rhythm-matching interaction with a handheld device is associated with reduced acute physiological arousal and physical restlessness in children. The study provides a preliminary baseline for future work examining how tactile robotic interactions may support calmness in more demanding or stressful contexts.

candidates.title: Understanding Newcomer Persistence in Social VR: A Case Study of VRChat
candidates.abstract: Newcomers are crucial for the growth of online communities, yet their successful integration into these spaces requires overcoming significant initial hurdles. Social Virtual Reality (VR) platforms are novel avenues that offer unprecedented online interaction experiences. Unlike well-studied two-dimensional online environments, the pathways to successful newcomer integration in online VR spaces are underexplored. Our research addresses this gap by examining the strategies used by newcomers to navigate early challenges in social VR and how they adapt. By focusing on active participants (ranging from newcomers currently navigating these hurdles to veterans who have successfully integrated) we isolate the specific strategies necessary for retention. We interviewed 24 active social VR users and conducted a reflexive thematic analysis. While participants identified barriers such as unfamiliar user interfaces, social norms, and overwhelming sensory input, our analysis reveals the adaptation strategies required to overcome them. Our findings expand on understanding newcomer persistence beyond traditional 2D environments, emphasizing how social dynamics influence the management of VR-specific issues like VR sickness during onboarding. Additionally, we highlight how successful newcomers overcome the lack of clear objectives in social VR by proactively constructing social meaning. We propose design suggestions to scaffold these successful integration pathways.

candidates.title: Anthropomorphic Characters as Communication Agents in Mobile Banking:
candidates.abstract: This research examines how anthropomorphic characters can function as communication agents in mobile banking interfaces.Study 1 surveyed 485 users across Generations X, Y, and Z to compare their expected and actual mobile banking experiences.The results revealed substantial expectation gaps in security, professionalism, service fluency, and convenience, with Generation Z generally demonstrating greater unmet expectations regarding seamless and engaging service experiences.Study 2 conducted an exploratory eye-tracking experiment with Generation Y and Generation Z users to compare plain-text and character-assisted messages across utilitarian and hedonic mobile banking tasks.The findings suggest that usersʼ attention was primarily guided by task relevance.Anthropomorphic characters attracted limited attention when used as peripheral interface elements but became effective communication agents when directly associated with concise, task-relevant messages.Character-assisted communication showed a preliminary pattern of greater visual salience in hedonic task contexts.Together, the findings provide exploratory evidence that the value of anthropomorphic characters lies not merely in visual appeal but in their capacity to support customer communication at appropriate moments in the service journey.This research contributes to mobile service experience and anthropomorphic communication research and offers practical guidance for designing generationally responsive financial interfaces.

candidates.title: Local shocks and internal migration: The disparate effects of robots and Chinese imports in the US
candidates.abstract: Migration is a key mechanism through which local labor markets adjust to economic shocks. In this paper, we analyze the migration response of American workers to two of the most important shocks that hit US manufacturing since the 1990s: Chinese import competition and the introduction of industrial robots. Exploiting plausibly exogenous variation in exposure across US local labor markets over time, we establish a new fact. Even though both shocks drastically reduced employment in the manufacturing sector, only robots led to a sizable decline in population size. We provide evidence that negative employment spillovers outside manufacturing, caused by robots but not by Chinese imports, can explain the different migration responses. We interpret our findings through the lens of a model that highlights two mechanisms: the cost savings that each shock provides and the degree of complementarity between directly and indirectly exposed industries.

candidates.title: "I Just Don't Want My Work Being Fed Into The AI Blender": Queer Artists on Refusing and Resisting Generative AI
candidates.abstract: Art-making is a collective social activity through which queer people engage in political resistance, develop identities, archive queer memory, and form community. However, in recent years, generative AI has disrupted queer artistic communities. Through 15 semi-structured interviews, we examine how queer artists are making sense of the encroachment of GenAI into their art worlds. Our findings surface significant tensions between the relationality of our participants’ queer art practices and the perceived anti-relationality of GenAI development and use. We detail how our participants refuse and resist GenAI use and development in response and highlight the limited role our participants saw for GenAI within art-making, such as the queer aesthetic potential of surreal image models. Drawing on queer theory, we discuss how CSCW researchers might support queer artists by refusing dominant AI imaginaries and supporting queer world-building.
